msa_handling: **NOT APPLICABLE in the predictive sense — no MSA is built and no alignment depth is manipulated.** A *sequence* alignment does exist, but its only job is to transfer GPCRdb generic residue numbers onto each PDB entry: "using the Uniprot protein ID included in the answer, we re-retrieved the generic numbering of each protein from GPCRdb … a pairwise alignment of the structure and protein sequence was performed using the PairwiseAligner tool in Biopython. The parameters used were a match score of 2, a mismatch score of −1, and an internal_gap_open_score of −10. All other options were left at the default value of −1." (p.9) With the filter: "Only contiguous parts of the structures' sequences (according to residue numbering, ignoring gaps less than 10 in length) with at least 10 amino acid residues were independently aligned to the protein sequence. If the matched score was less than half the sequence length, the part was considered an addition to the sequence and was ignored." (p.9) This is neither subsampling nor state-filtering; do not collapse it into either.
states_generated: **NOT APPLICABLE — nothing is generated.** 1351 deposited structures are projected onto one learned coordinate (G_CA = PC1) and partitioned into two classes by a 1-D GMM (pp.10–11). The *analysed* state handling is **two-state**: "we used a one-dimensional GMM on the first principal component and decomposed the data into two classes." (p.10); "The analysis confirms that there are two distinct states for the inactive and active conformations." (p.7). Intermediates are acknowledged as existing in the annotation and then dropped: "Structures reported as 'intermediate' or 'other' have been ignored because their number is too low to be distinguished from the graph." (p.2, Fig. 1 caption). One continuum-like object is produced but only as a visualisation, not as structures: the Supplementary Movie interpolates along PC1 "from low (inactive) to high (active) values" (p.12) — interpolated Cα coordinates, explicitly a linear interpolation in the PCA subspace, not sampled conformations.
structural_priors_used: **The entire input is deposited experimental structures carrying database state annotations. This is the design, not a defect.** Enumerated: 1. **Database supplying the structures and the labels: GPCRdb.** "The structural data used in this work were collected from the curated GPCRdb database (Isberg et al., 2015). We collected all class A GPCRs from GPCRdb, assembling a total of 1010 PDB structures, filtering out only those that did not have a downloadable PDB file in the RCSB PDB." (p.8). Files themselves from the RCSB PDB (p.9). **Counts: 1010 for model building; 1006 train + 345 held-out = 1351 total in the final analysis (Supp. Tables 1–3, p.22).** 2. **State annotations come from GPCRdb, not from the authors.** "Data identifiers are from GPCRdb, as listed for each structure … Annual deposits broken down by the activation state reported by GPCRdb, considering 'active' (in blue) and 'inactive' (orange) states." (p.2, Fig. 1 caption). The ligand-class labels (agonist / antagonist / inverse agonist / partial agonist / none) and the G-protein-bound flag that define every series in Fig. 2 are likewise GPCRdb annotations (p.4; Supp. Table 3, p.22). 3. **Generic residue numbering from GPCRdb** is the featurisation backbone: "To featurize the data, we used the generic numbering of GPCR residues provided by GPCRdb." (p.9) 4. **An active-state reference structure, 3P0G**, is used for rigid-body removal and as the visual "genuine active" comparator in Fig. 3: "using the structure 3P0G (Rasmussen et al., 2011) as the reference" (pp.9, 10); "TM6 and TM7 of the genuine active-state structure (3P0G) in red" (p.7, Fig. 3 caption). 5. **The active/inactive anchor classes are defined by biochemistry known in advance**: G-protein + agonist bound = active; antagonist without G protein = inactive. "In this framework, structures bound to both G protein and agonist simultaneously correspond to the active state of the GPCR. Structures bound only to antagonist (without G protein) are predominantly in the inactive state." (p.4) 6. **Prior activation indices are cited as the standard against which the new one is positioned** — the A100 index ("a linear combination of five inter-helix distances developed for class A GPCR proteins. It was trained on simulation data and validated on 268 experimental structures from the PDB", p.3) and the GPCRdb percentage-of-activation model ("structures are classified as fully inactive if a condition based on a certain distance between TM2 and TM6 is met, while fully active structures are G protein or arrestin-bound structures", p.3). Neither is used as a feature. 7. **Simulation priors are explicitly excluded**, which is the paper's stated methodological selling point: "given that the model utilizes only experimental structural data, potential problems that might arise from including simulation data as part of the analysis are avoided." (p.11)
oracle_leakage: **Not a prediction pipeline, so routes 1, 3 and 5 are answered on their own terms; the live routes are 2, 4, 6 and 7. Headline: the model is unsupervised in its *fitting* and label-driven in its *component selection, orientation and validation*, and the paper then declares a subset of those same labels wrong.** Route by route. **Route 1 — deposited structures used as input or template: PRESENT BY CONSTRUCTION, and it is the object of study, not a contaminant.** Every datum is a deposited structure; there is nothing to leak *into*, because nothing is predicted. Protocol on p.8 (Data collection and featurization) and p.10 (Structural index G_CA). Verbatim: "The machine learning (ML)-based model we developed utilizes only experimental structural data from the PDB, thus avoiding the sampling limitations of atomistic simulations." (p.3) **Route 2 — state annotations from a curated database (GPCRdb) driving templates or alignments: PRESENT, in a specific and limited way — GPCRdb annotations do not enter the PCA/GMM fit, but they select and orient the index and then validate it.** - The generic numbering (a GPCRdb product, not a state annotation) drives the alignment and the feature set: "To featurize the data, we used the generic numbering of GPCR residues provided by GPCRdb." (p.9) - The *state/ligand* annotations drive which principal component becomes the index: "The choice of the first component to calculate the index is based on our previous observation in Supplementary Fig. 4, which shows that the first component is able to distinguish active GPCR structures bound to G protein from inactive ones." (p.10) - And they supply the validation: "Figure 2 shows that the G_CA index distinguishes antagonist-bound structures from structures bound to both G protein and agonist … This confirms that the index serves as a reliable proxy of receptor activation." (p.4) - **The circularity to record**: the same annotation set that selected PC1 and certified it as "a reliable proxy of receptor activation" (p.4) is then declared wrong where it disagrees with the index: "All these structures are marked as active in the GPCRdb classification." (p.6) and "If any experimental structure was initially misinterpreted and labeled, the model can identify and correct it." (p.11). The paper offers independent structural evidence for those seven cases (Fig. 3, p.7), which is the right move — but no independent evidence anywhere for the agreement cases. **Route 3 — cluster labels derived from known states: NONE FOUND at fit time; PRESENT at interpretation time.** The GMM is fitted without labels — "Gaussian mixture models (GMM) were used to find explicit categories in the reduced dimensional space. Specifically, we used a one-dimensional GMM on the first principal component and decomposed the data into two classes." (p.10) — but *which* of the two clusters is "active" is assigned from the known ligand/G-protein annotations (p.4, quoted above). Choosing k = 2 also encodes the prior that there are exactly two functional states. **Route 4 — hyperparameters, sweep ranges, seeds or stopping criteria tuned against known states: PRESENT, twice, and once benignly.** - *Component selection against the evaluation labels* (the real instance): PC1 out of five candidate components is chosen because it separates the labelled classes — "only the first component distinguishes antagonist-bound vs. G protein and agonist-bound structures. This strongly suggests that only the first component indicates activation." (p.10) and again p.10 in the index definition. Per schema route 4 this is model selection made against the labels the model is later scored on, and it is leakage even though no per-structure value is tuned. Mitigating: the PCA itself is fitted with no labels, only one of five components is in play, and Supp. Fig. 3 shows the variance falls below 5% per component after the fifth (pp.9–10), so the choice is heavily constrained by the data alone. - *KDE bandwidth chosen for appearance*: "The distributions in Fig. 2 were calculated as kernel density estimates using the kdeplot function of the seaborn package, with the bw_adjust parameter set to 0.5 to achieve a higher resolution distribution." (p.10). The paper's central minority-peak claim ("the observed minority peak is significant", p.7) is read off exactly these smoothed curves. Underlying histograms are relegated to Supp. Fig. 6 (p.21). Not state-label tuning, but it is a display parameter tuned in the direction of the finding; recorded in `hides` on the Fig. 2 row. - *Threshold*: **not** hand-tuned — it falls out of the GMM plus a bootstrap, see `state_metric`. **Route 5 — success defined post hoc by RMSD to a structure they had: NONE FOUND as a success criterion.** No RMSD-to-reference score is used to judge anything. RMSD appears only as the objective of the rigid-body superposition: "This step minimizes the root mean square deviation (RMSD) between all structures and the reference." (p.10). Protocol is on pp.9–10. The one caveat worth stating is that the reference for that superposition is an active-state structure (3P0G), so the coordinate frame is anchored on one end of the activation axis. **Route 6 — best/worst labels assigned against a held reference: PRESENT for the anomaly analysis, and assigned by eye.** The seven "mislabelled" structures are adjudicated by visual comparison against 3P0G: "a closer look at the G protein-binding site shown in Fig. 3 reveals that these structures share key features of the inactive conformation: TM6 remains close to the center of the helical bundle of a GPCR, while TM7 is shifted outward—both being hallmarks of the inactive state." (p.6). No G_CA value, no distance, no angle is reported for any of the seven. → tag `visual-metric` applies to this sub-result specifically. **Route 7 — design-level oracle use (weaker than pipeline leakage; kept distinct): PRESENT and explicit.** The expected answer is declared before the index is read. The active and inactive poles are defined by prior biochemistry ("structures bound to both G protein and agonist simultaneously correspond to the active state", p.4); the interpretation of the PC1 motion is checked against the textbook expectation and reported as agreement ("The outward movement of TM6 is the most important indicator of GPCR activation … This feature is a common denominator in structural data and is also reflected in our index.", p.5); and the paper's conclusion about G-protein-bound structures is stated as an expectation in the same breath as the evidence ("These structural anomalies suggest that there is no reason to expect G protein binding to receptors in an inactive conformation.", p.6). → tags `design-level-oracle` and `oracle-leak` (the latter for the route-4 component selection only).
prospective: **partial.** Prospective in one real sense and retrospective in the rest. - *Prospective element, genuine*: a frozen model was applied to structures that did not exist when it was built. "After training the model, the GPCRdb query was rerun, adding new structures published during the training phase to the analysis and updating some of the labels. The selection was kept static, and the model was not retrained with new data." (p.10) — 345 structures (Supp. Tables 1–3, p.22), analysed in Supp. Fig. 5 (p.20). - *Retrospective everywhere else*: the index is built on, selected against, and validated on the same annotated corpus, and every mechanistic conclusion is drawn from the distribution of already-deposited structures. There is no wet-lab measurement, no new structure, and no prediction tested against a later experiment.
state_metric: **Dual — continuous coordinate + binary predicate. And the descriptors are LEARNED, not the classical TM6/DRY/NPxxY geometry.** This matters, because the paper is a candidate source for a state predicate. - **The continuous coordinate** is G_CA, the projection of a structure's aligned Cα coordinates on the first PCA component: "G_CA = w_PC1 · (x_target − x̄)", where "w_PC1 are the weights of the first component of the PCA model, x_target are the aligned coordinates of the target structure, and x̄ are the mean coordinates of all structures" (p.10). Higher = more active. **Units are NOT REPORTED** (the weight vector is a unit vector and the coordinates are in Å, so the index carries Å, but the paper never says so and never labels the axis with units — Fig. 2, p.4). - **The feature set is backbone Cα only, at GPCRdb generic-numbered positions present in every structure**: "it utilizes only protein backbone coordinates from conserved structural features of the receptor transmembrane domain, ensuring its general applicability" (p.3); "Once the structures were aligned, generic numbers that appeared in all structures were selected for further analysis" (p.9); "The analysis was done on the alpha carbon coordinates of those residues that are not missing in any structure." (p.9, Fig. 4 caption). Explicitly **no side chains**: "the model does not include structural details of proteins, such as side chain orientations. This makes it insensitive to the interpretation problems of noisy experimental structural data" (p.11). **Therefore: no DRY motif geometry, no NPxxY geometry, no ionic-lock distance, no TM3–TM6 or TM2–TM6 distance is measured anywhere in this paper.** The classical distance-based indices are described only as prior art to be improved on (A100, five inter-helix distances; GPCRdb TM2–TM6 condition — both p.3). - **The number of residues in the selected set is NOT REPORTED**, and neither are the generic numbers themselves. Fig. 4b (p.9) shows the selection graphically (green = present in all structures, orange = missing in at least one) but gives no count and no list. - **The binary predicate is a threshold on G_CA at −1.72, with a stated confidence interval**: "Structures bound to both G protein and agonist (Fig. 2b, blue line) are predominantly found with index values above –1.72, while G protein-free and antagonist-bound structures (Fig. 2a, orange) are mainly found below this threshold. Thus, index values above –1.72 define the active region, while values below this threshold define the inactive region." (p.4). Exact value with uncertainty: "**With a 95% confidence interval, this resulted in a threshold value of –1.72 ± 0.44, with the active region defined as index values greater than this threshold.**" (p.11) - **Threshold justification — REPORTED and reasonable.** It is not hand-picked: it is the decision boundary of a two-component 1-D GMM fitted on PC1, with the uncertainty from bootstrap resampling: "To estimate uncertainty of the threshold index, we performed bootstrapping analysis by generating resampled data sets from the original data and rebuilding the GMM. To obtain a robust estimate and minimize the statistical error, we used 10,000 resampled data sets." (pp.10–11). What is *not* justified is the choice of two components in the mixture (k = 2 is asserted, never selected by BIC/AIC or any model-selection criterion). - **Missing-residue handling** has a closed-form estimator (Supplementary Data, p.15): Ĝ_CA = G_N / Σ_{i∈N} w_i², i.e. the partial index divided by the retained weight mass. Claimed robust without numbers: "the error estimate depends on which residue is missing, but even if several residues are missing, the error remains relatively small." (p.10). No error magnitude is given for any number of missing residues. - **Reimplementability: NO, from this PDF.** The predicate is `G_CA > −1.72`, but G_CA needs the PC1 weight vector, the mean coordinate vector, the residue selection list and the 3P0G superposition — none of which are in the paper, and no repository URL is given despite three "openly available" claims (pp.1, 3, 8). - → tags `continuous-metric`, `binary-predicate`, and `visual-metric` for the Fig. 3 anomaly adjudication.
metric_saturation: **No numeric saturation.** G_CA is an unbounded projection; it neither floors nor ceilings in any reported arm (observed range roughly −18 to +10 across Fig. 2a–b, p.4, and Supp. Fig. 5, p.20). The binary predicate is one-sided, so any structure far into the active region is indistinguishable from one just over −1.72, but that is a consequence of thresholding, not saturation of the underlying measure — and the continuous values are always shown alongside. The bounded quantity in the paper is the KDE density on the y-axis, which is a display normalisation, not a measurement. Figure-level display issues (categories omitted from Fig. 2, partial-year bar in Fig. 1, bandwidth choice) are recorded in `hides` on the relevant figure rows, per v3 rule 9.
directional_control: **NOT APPLICABLE as a method property — there is nothing to instruct, because nothing is generated.** The paper's substantive result is nonetheless *about* which physical handle controls state occupancy, and that is the reusable content: the handles are (i) **ligand class**, which shifts the population but leaves it bimodal, and (ii) **G protein binding**, which is the only handle that collapses the population onto the active state. "Interestingly, structures bound to G protein but not to agonist, and structures bound to agonist but without G protein, are distributed over a broad front along the index, although both have a peak in the active region that represents the primary state." (pp.4–5); "when we studied the structures of G protein-bound receptors, we found that they almost unambiguously represent only the active state, suggesting that the function of G protein is to lock the receptor in the active state." (p.7). Antagonists and inverse agonists act as the opposite-direction handle: "antagonists attenuate the dynamics of their receptor along the activation coordinate, stabilizing the inactive state … inverse agonists act as stronger inactivators than antagonists" (p.5).
anti_memorization_design: **YES — a temporally held-out set of 345 structures, defined by deposition/annotation after the model was frozen.** "After training the model, the GPCRdb query was rerun, adding new structures published during the training phase to the analysis and updating some of the labels. The selection was kept static, and the model was not retrained with new data. Eight of the new structures were ignored because they were missing a residue from the list." (p.10). n = 345 (Supp. Tables 1–3, p.22: 1351 total − 1006 train). **The cutoff is defined by "during the training phase", not by a date** — no calendar cutoff is stated anywhere, which makes the split unreproducible by anyone else. Composition of the held-out set (Supp. Table 1, p.22): aminergic 132, peptide 74, lipid 47, orphan 31, protein 19, alicarboxylic acid 19, nucleotide 8, sensory 7, steroid 6, other 2, melatonin 0; by species (Supp. Table 2): human 326, HCMV 8, bovine 3, mouse 3, *Hasarius adansoni* 3, HHV-8 2.
anti_memorization_control: **RUN and analysed, not merely existing; adequately powered (n = 345), but reported with no number.** The frozen model was applied to the new structures and the result is a figure: "Supplementary Fig. 5 summarizes the analysis of the new structures." (p.10); Supp. Fig. 5 caption: "Results of the data not used for training." (p.20). Displayed series and n (read from the rendered panel, p.20): panel a (no G protein) agonist N = 45, antagonist N = 21, inverse agonist N = 13; panel b (with G protein) agonist N = 236, none N = 18 — 333 of the 345. The held-out distributions visibly reproduce the training-set pattern (agonist-without-G-protein peaked in the active region with an inactive shoulder; G-protein-bound almost entirely active). **What is missing is any quantity**: no agreement rate with GPCRdb labels, no classification accuracy, no distributional test between train and held-out, and no sentence in the main text stating what the held-out arm showed. The control was run; its result was never scored. NOT `UNPOWERED` (n = 345, no overlap with training by construction).
confidence_as_discriminator: **NOT APPLICABLE — there is no predictor and therefore no pLDDT/pTM/ipTM.** The paper's only confidence-like quantities are statistical, not model-internal: the bootstrap 95% CI on the threshold (−1.72 ± 0.44, p.11) and the qualitative missing-residue error claim (p.10). Neither is used to judge conformational correctness of an individual structure. Experimental confidence measures (map resolution, B-factors, model-to-map fit) are **NOT REPORTED** and are not used to filter or weight any structure — a notable omission given the anomaly conclusion (p.6) rests on structure quality.
stance: **`precedent` (on findings) + `contrast` (on rigour and reproducibility). Provisional — the user's call.** - *Precedent*: this is an independent, experiment-only statement that agonist binding shifts the population but does not lock it, and that a stable active state is established only on G protein binding — asserted repeatedly and quotably (claims 1–7 above), on 1351 deposited structures. For any argument that a conformationally correct active-state model requires the transducer rather than the agonist, this is the structural-database precedent. - *Contrast*: the index is selected and validated against the same GPCRdb annotations it is then used to correct; there is no classification performance number anywhere (no accuracy, no AUC, no agreement rate — not even for the held-out arm that was run); the seven "mislabelled" structures are adjudicated by eye with no index values reported; the "openly available" tool has no URL; and the Methods are explicitly withheld pending acceptance. A corpus argument about operationalised state predicates can use this paper as an example of a predicate that is well-posed in principle (GMM + bootstrap CI) and unreproducible in practice.
n_predictions: **NOT APPLICABLE — no structures are predicted or sampled.** The equivalent scale figures: **1010** structures used to build the PCA/GMM (p.8, p.10); **1006** training and **345** held-out structures in the final analysis, **1351** total (p.22); **10,000** bootstrap resamples for the threshold CI (pp.10–11); **1** interpolation trajectory along PC1 (Supplementary Movie, p.12). Structures per receptor and number of distinct receptors are **NOT REPORTED** — the tables aggregate to subfamily, species and Gα type only.
si_in_scope: **SI IS HELD — the supplementary material is bound into this PDF, pages 15–22.** It contains the missing-residue derivation (Supplementary Data, p.15), Supplementary Figs. 1–6 (pp.16–21) and Supplementary Tables 1–3 (p.22, the source of every structure count above). Two things are *not* held: (i) the **Supplementary Movie** (p.12), which is the only presentation of the PC1 interpolation and therefore the only place the TM6/TM7 motion is actually shown; (ii) the **code and the fitted model** — the tool is called "openly available" three times (pp.1, 3, 8) with no URL, no repository, no DOI and no data-availability section anywhere in the PDF, so the PC1 weight vector, the mean coordinate vector and the residue selection list needed to compute G_CA are all absent. Also note the SI listing on p.11 is internally inconsistent: "Additional results: Supplementary Figure 1-6, 1-8, Supplementary Table 1-3" — only Figs. 1–6 exist in the document.

year: 2024 (issue). Received 22 September 2023; revised 27 October 2023; accepted 30 October 2023; **advance access 24 November 2023** (p.1, p.10).
venue: *Nucleic Acids Research* 2024, **52**, D466–D475, **Database issue**. **Peer-reviewed, not a preprint** — the paper carries a full editorial record ("Received: September 22, 2023. Revised: October 27, 2023. Editorial Decision: October 28, 2023. Accepted: October 30, 2023", p.1 and p.10) and is published by Oxford University Press on behalf of NAR. → tag `peer-reviewed`.
title: GproteinDb in 2024: new G protein-GPCR couplings, AlphaFold2-multimer models and interface interactions
system: **GPCR** — specifically GPCR–heterotrimeric G protein complexes and their intracellular coupling interface. Receptor classes A (Rhodopsin), B1 (Secretin), B2 (Adhesion), C (Glutamate), F (Frizzled) and T (Taste 2) (p.5). "There are 16 human G proteins grouped in four families" — Gs (Gs, Golf), Gi/o (Gi1, Gi2, Gi3, Go, Gz, Gt1, Gt2, Ggust), Gq/11 (Gq, G11, G14, G15) and G12/13 (G12, G13) (p.1).
n_targets: **Five distinct counts; do not collapse them.** - *Modelled interactome*: **425 human GPCRs × 16 human Gα subunits = 6,800 theoretical complexes**, of which **5,595 (82%)** have released models (p.5, p.8). - *Primary-transducer complex models with Gαβγ*: **1,121** (p.4, Results) — but the Methods on p.3 say **1,124** ("1124 such models completed at time of writing"). See `unresolved` item 1. - *Experimental structures curated*: "There are currently 690 G protein structures, whereof 544 are structures of GPCR - G protein complexes." (p.4). The interface tool previously covered **527** structures (p.6). - *Coupling-agreement analyses*: **50** shared GPCRs (Fig. 4A), **18** GPCRs with constitutive couplings (Fig. 4B), **66** shared GPCRs giving **79** GPCR–primary-transducer combinations (Fig. 4C–D) (pp.7–8). - *Previous release for contrast*: **3,081** MODELLER homology models (p.8).
method_class: **other (curated database resource) + co-folding (production use of an off-the-shelf predictor).** No new predictor, no new sampling scheme, no benchmark. AlphaFold2-Multimer is run at interactome scale and the outputs are served through a web platform with visualisation and analysis tools. `benchmark-only` is explicitly **wrong**: nothing is benchmarked.
backbones: **AlphaFold2 only** — "All models were built using AlphaFold2 version 2.3.1 with the Multimer option and amber relaxation (27)." (p.3). Single backbone, **not** `multi-backbone`. Other structural tooling: MODELLER for refining experimental structures (p.3); D3/Javascript, Python/Django for visualisation (p.3).
templates: **on, with a date cutoff, not state-annotated.** "Structural templates were included up to 1 January 2023." (p.3). No template curation, no state annotation, no per-target template selection is described. → tag `templates-on`. Note the **reverse direction** as well: the AF2M models are themselves used as templates to complete experimental structures — "instead of using experimental structures of other receptors, the AlphaFold2-Multimer model of the same receptor is used as swap-in template to fill in missing coordinates of Gα proteins and receptors" (p.3).
msa_handling: **NOT REPORTED.** The strings "MSA", "multiple sequence alignment", "subsample", "cluster" (of alignments) and "sequence database" do not appear anywhere in pp.1–8 in connection with the AF2M runs. Default AF2-Multimer v2.3.1 behaviour is the only reasonable inference and is therefore **not** recorded as a value. The only sequence engineering described is at the *input construct* level: ICL3 shortened to 14 residues for class A, GPS-site and N-terminal truncations for class B2, and VFTD deletion for class C (p.3).
states_generated: **one.** One AF2-Multimer complex model per GPCR–Gα (or GPCR–Gαβγ) pair is released. No ensemble is retained, no alternative receptor conformation is sought, and no second state of any receptor appears anywhere. **How many AF2M models were generated per complex, and by what rule one was chosen for release, is NOT REPORTED** — the words "seed", "recycle", "ranked" and "5 models" do not appear (pp.3, 5). The receptor conformation in these models is never named: all models are Gα-bound and therefore *implicitly* active-like, but the paper never states or checks this. → tag `single-state`.
structural_priors_used: **Extensive, disclosed, and not a defect — this is what a resource paper is made of.** - *Deposited structures as AF2M templates*: "Structural templates were included up to 1 January 2023." (p.3). - *The PDB itself*: "The Structures page is updated quarterly with new structures from the Protein Data Bank (structures from RCSB (43) and SIFTs data from PDBe (14))" (p.4), giving 690 G protein structures / 544 GPCR–G protein complexes (p.4). - *Refined experimental structures*, built with MODELLER and completed using the AF2M models of the same receptor as swap-in templates (p.3) — a deliberate model→structure feedback that the note flags under `oracle_leakage` route 1. - *Curated coupling datasets choose the modelled partner*: "We build models of GPCRs with the heterotrimeric G proteins that have been identified as the primary transducer from one of the quantitative coupling datasets in GproteinDb" (p.3). The datasets are GtoPdb (1), Inoue TGFα shedding (5), Inoue NanoBiT-G (5), Bouvier GEMTA/EMTA (4), Martemyanov FreeGβγ-Nluc (25) and Lambert RGB-GDP (22–24) (pp.2, 4). - *GPCRdb* supplies the 425-receptor set and the receptor generic residue numbering (pp.3, 4, 5). - *Common Gα numbering (CGN) scheme* (33) supplies the G protein residue coordinate system used by the superposition tool and every interface analysis (pp.3, 4). - *Interaction definitions* are imported wholesale from the GPCRdb structure-analysis platform: "strict and loose definitions, respectively (from (46), defined in a tool tip)" (pp.5, 6).
oracle_leakage: **Answered per route. There is no held-out reference set and no scored prediction anywhere in this paper, so routes 5 and 6 have nothing to leak into. The one genuine circularity is in the *coupling-agreement* analysis, not in the structure pipeline.** **Route 1 — deposited structures used as input or template: PRESENT, by design, and bidirectional.** Templates are on to 1 January 2023 (p.3), so any GPCR–G protein complex deposited before that date can template its own model. The reverse leak is stated explicitly and is more unusual — the models are then used to complete the experimental structures they were templated from: > "We updated our refined complex structures from (11) to use our AlphaFold2-Multimer complex models (next section). Hence, instead of using experimental structures of other receptors, the AlphaFold2-Multimer model of the same receptor is used as swap-in template to fill in missing coordinates of Gα proteins and receptors." (p.3) This matters downstream: the "refined structures" served by GproteinDb are **part experimental, part AF2M model**, and the interface interactions counted on them (Fig. 3D) include model-derived atoms. Anyone consuming GproteinDb refined structures as ground truth is consuming AF2M output in part. **Route 2 — state annotations from a curated database driving templates or alignments: NONE FOUND.** No state annotation of any kind enters the pipeline. GproteinDb's own curated annotations that *are* used are **coupling** annotations (which partner to model, p.3) and **residue-numbering** schemes (GPCRdb generic numbers, CGN, pp.3–4) — neither is a conformational-state label. The full model-building protocol is on p.3 ("Building GPCR–G protein complex structure models") and names only: sequences, the Multimer option, amber relaxation, a template date cutoff, and construct truncations. Note for the corpus: the *sister* resource GPCRdb does hold state annotations — ref. 2 is titled "GPCRdb in 2023: state-specific structure models using AlphaFold2" (p.9) — but **GproteinDb's models here carry none**. See `unresolved` item 7. **Route 3 — cluster labels derived from known states: NONE FOUND.** No clustering of structures or models is performed anywhere. Protocol pp.2–3. **Route 4 — hyperparameters, thresholds or stopping criteria tuned against known answers: PRESENT, twice, and the second is genuine circularity.** *(4a) Model quality thresholds were set by eye on the outputs themselves.* Verbatim, p.3: > "We established thresholds for pTM ≥0.5 and ipTM ≥0.2, both ranging from 0 to 1, with 1 signifying a highly accurate model. This choice was guided by our examination of the relative positioning of the Gα and GPCR, with emphasis on preventing loop knots. A pTM cutoff of ≥0.5 indicated good overall model quality and enabled us to adopt a more permissive ipTM (≥0.2). This approach ensured the expected positioning of the Gα relative to the GPCR." The only external justification offered is for pTM ≥0.5: "These cut-offs are consistent with the levels of significance on the TM scores identified in previous studies assessing protein fold similarity (28)." (p.3). The ipTM ≥0.2 and the PAE-mean ≤26 Å cutoffs ("with PAE scores ranging from 0 to 31.75 Å, we established a cut-off of 26 Å for the PAE mean score of compared residues (even if the ipTM score was satisfactory)", p.3) rest on the authors' visual inspection. **No experimental structure is used to calibrate any of them** — so this is tuning against an *expectation*, not against a reference set, which is weaker than classical leakage but leaves the gate unvalidated. *(4b) The coupling cutoff was chosen to maximise the agreement that is later reported as a result.* Methods, p.2: > "For the Inoue TGFα shedding dataset we also applied a cutoff log(Emax/EC50 ) ≥ 7.0, which were based on the largest agreement with couplings and non-couplings determined by both the Bouvier GEMTA and Martemyanov FreeGβγ-Nluc datasets." Discussion, p.6, reporting that same agreement as a finding: > "To account for excessive signal amplification from the TGF-α shedding biosensor, we applied a filter requiring log(Emax/EC50 ≥ 7.0). Notably, this achieves an agreement of 94% for couplings and 82% for non-couplings between Gq and GPCRs compared to the EMTA/GEMTA and FreeGβγ-Nluc datasets (Figure 4A)." The threshold was selected to maximise agreement with those two datasets and the resulting agreement with those two datasets is then presented as a headline number and as Figure 4A. The 94% / 82% are therefore **fitted, not measured**, and should never be quoted as independent cross-biosensor concordance. → tag `oracle-leak` (scoped to the coupling analysis, not to a structure benchmark). **Route 5 — success defined post hoc by RMSD or TM to a structure they had: NONE FOUND.** Model acceptance is defined entirely by AlphaFold's own self-confidence (pTM, ipTM, PAE mean) and by pLDDT visualisation (p.3, p.5). The strings "RMSD", "TM-score to", "DockQ" and "reference structure" never appear in an evaluative sense; the only TM discussion is the definition of pTM/ipTM (p.3). **No model is ever compared to an experimental complex anywhere in the paper.** **Route 6 — best/worst model labels assigned against a held reference: NONE FOUND.** No model is labelled good or bad relative to any experimental structure; there is no per-model accuracy claim at all (pp.3, 5). **Route 7 — design-level oracle use: PRESENT but mild, and the authors run the non-oracle arm alongside it.** For the 1,121/1,124 heterotrimeric models the partner is chosen because it is the *experimentally determined* primary transducer — "the heterotrimeric G proteins that have been identified as the primary transducer from one of the quantitative coupling datasets in GproteinDb" (p.3). That is answer-conditioned system selection. **However**, the far larger 5,595-model arm is deliberately exhaustive over all 6,800 theoretical pairs and is therefore free of it, and the authors argue for that choice explicitly: > "We choose to model all theoretical G protein–GPCR complexes, as it is difficult to definitely rule out specific complexes that cannot form. For example, a complex not observed in one experiment may form in another experiment if changing the cell line or ligand (system and ligand bias, respectively)." (p.8) → tag `design-level-oracle`, scoped to the primary-transducer subset.
prospective: **NOT APPLICABLE.** The category presupposes a prediction that is later checked. Nothing here is scored against a withheld answer, before or after the fact. The resource *serves* models for others to test; it tests none itself. Recording `no` would falsely imply a retrospective evaluation was run.
state_metric: **NOT REPORTED — and this is the single most important negative in the note.** The resource **does not assign, annotate, or verify a receptor activation state for any of its 5,595 (or 1,121) models**, and offers no criterion by which one could be called. Evidence, exhaustive over pp.1–8: the strings "active state", "inactive", "conformation", "conformational", "TM6", "apo", "agonist-bound" and "state-specific" do not appear in connection with any model. The only occurrence of "state" in the whole body text is a reference to the field's selectivity debate — "transient intermediate-state complexes (52)" (p.8) — and the only occurrences of "activ-" are pharmacological (constitutive activity, agonist-induced activity, activation rate, Adhesion-receptor self-activation, p.1, p.3, p.4, p.8). Every quality metric offered (pTM, ipTM, PAE mean, pLDDT, pp.3, 5) scores **model confidence and Gα placement**, never receptor conformation. The models are all G protein-bound and so are implicitly active-like, but that is an inference the reader must supply; the paper never makes it. **Any downstream use of GproteinDb models as "active-state" structures is importing an annotation the resource does not provide.**
metric_saturation: **No numeric saturation is reported, because no distribution of any metric is shown.** The paper reports not a single distribution, mean or spread of pTM, ipTM, PAE or pLDDT over the 5,595 models; only the threshold values and the fact that 1,205 of 6,800 complexes fail them (pp.3, 5, 8). Two ceiling-adjacent points worth recording: (i) Figure 4B's headline "17 (94%)" agreement is **one discordant receptor away from its 100% ceiling at n = 18** (p.8), so the metric is effectively at ceiling on a very small denominator; (ii) the ipTM ≥0.2 gate sits so low in the 0–1 range that it is near the metric's *floor* rather than a discriminating threshold, which the authors acknowledge as "a more permissive ipTM" (p.3). Neither is an axis artefact — figure-level defects are in `hides`.
directional_control: **Partner identity is the only handle, and it controls the complex, not the receptor state.** Each model is built by naming which Gα (or Gαβγ) sequence is co-folded with which receptor sequence (p.3). Everything else in the schema's handle list is **absent**: no ligand or agonist is ever supplied (see below), no nanobody, no G-protein mimetic, no state-annotated template, no state-filtered MSA, no seed or subsample-depth control. Two construct-level manipulations exist but are clash-avoidance, not direction: ICL3 shortened to 14 residues in class A, and — decisively for any ligand reading — "as were Class C GPCRs (removing the large ligand-binding Venus Flytrap domain (VFTD))" (p.3), i.e. the class C models cannot bind their orthosteric ligand at all. → tag `partner-driven`. **On ligands and agonists, stated precisely because the question was asked.** The paper **never states, either way, whether a ligand or agonist was included in the AlphaFold2-Multimer inputs → NOT REPORTED.** What can be quoted is that every enumeration of what goes into a model names protein chains only: "models of GPCRs with the heterotrimeric G proteins" (p.3); "structure models of 1121 GPCRs and heterotrimeric G proteins" (p.4); "5595 models of the 16 human Gα subunits and 425 human GPCRs in GPCRdb" (p.5); "models of the theoretical interactome spanning all 16 human Gα subunits and 425 human GPCRs" (Fig. 2 caption, p.5). The word "ligand" appears eleven times in pp.1–8 and **not once in the model-building Methods**: it appears in pharmacology framing (biased ligands, ligand bias, ligand types, endogenous ligand, pp.1, 4, 5, 8), as a curated *annotation field on experimental PDB structures* — "ligand (name, type, PubChem ID, modality)" (p.4) — and in the VFTD deletion above (p.3). "Agonist" appears only as an assay condition in the coupling datasets (pp.4, 7, 8), never as a modelling input. So: **inferable as ligand-free, but recorded as NOT REPORTED because the paper does not say it.**
anti_memorization_design: **NONE.** A template date cutoff exists — "Structural templates were included up to 1 January 2023." (p.3) — but it is a **data freeze on template availability, not a held-out evaluation set**: no complexes are set aside, no post-cutoff subset is defined, and n = 0. AlphaFold2 v2.3.1's own training cutoff is never stated, so the memorization status of the 544 deposited complexes that overlap the modelled set is unknown and unknowable from this PDF. → tag `no-anti-memorization`.
anti_memorization_control: **NONE RUN.** No arm of any kind is run on recent, post-cutoff or held-out structures. There is no accuracy evaluation to run one in.
confidence_as_discriminator: **YES, as the sole release criterion, and never validated.** pTM, ipTM and PAE mean decide which of the 6,800 theoretical complexes are published: "the remainder will be added in coming releases as they pass our quality filters (see Methods)" (p.5); "more models will be added as they pass our quality filters" (p.8). pLDDT is served per residue in the 3D viewer and the three scores are shown as horizontal bars against their range limits (p.5). The authors' own summary claim is strong: "Together, this comprehensive system grants users a swift, yet in-depth perspective on the quality and reliability of the G protein-GPCR complex models." (p.5). **No validation of that use is performed** — the confidence scores are never correlated with, or checked against, any experimental structure, any coupling label, or any other independent quantity. The gate is calibrated by the authors' visual inspection alone (route 4a). It is a *quaternary-placement* discriminator (is Gα positioned as expected relative to the GPCR), never a receptor-conformation discriminator. → tag `confidence-as-discriminator`.
stance: **`background` + `precedent` — provisional, the user's call.**
n_predictions: - *Targets*: 425 human GPCRs × 16 human Gα = 6,800 theoretical complexes; plus 1,121 (or 1,124) GPCR–Gαβγ primary-transducer complexes. - *Total models released*: 5,595 Gα–GPCR models + 1,121 heterotrimeric models. Whether the heterotrimeric set is disjoint from the 5,595 is not stated. - *Samples per target*: **NOT REPORTED.** The number of AF2M seeds, recycles or candidate models per complex, and the rule for selecting the released one, are never given (p.3). Any per-target sampling comparison against our numbers is therefore impossible from this PDF. - *Total models generated (as opposed to released)*: **NOT REPORTED** — 1,205 complexes are said to fail the filters, but whether models were generated and discarded, or never generated, is not stated.
si_in_scope: **SI NOT HELD — and the gap is large.** The paper has no supplementary figures or tables at all; its underlying numbers live outside the PDF. Specifically: (i) "The MS Excel file containing all coupling datasets and their processing for import into GproteinDb can be downloaded via a link in the Couplings page." (p.3), and "the Couplings page provides a link to the MS Excel file via which all couplings were imported to GproteinDb and containing additional raw data, formulas (for normalizations, cut-offs etc.) and statistical significances (SDs or SEMs) not shown online." (p.4); (ii) Fig. 4's underlying data: "The underlying datasets and calculations of above agreements are available in the file GPCR-G_protein_couplings.xlsx available from the Couplings page." (p.7); (iii) Zenodo records 10174368 (code) and 10168935 (data files) (p.8); (iv) the chimera-to-wildtype alignment FASTA on GitHub (p.3). **The per-model pTM/ipTM/PAE/pLDDT values, the distribution of those scores over 5,595 models, and the identity of the 1,205 excluded complexes exist only in the live resource, not in any file this corpus holds.** Anyone wanting model-quality statistics must pull them from gproteindb.org or the Zenodo deposit.

year: 2026 — "this version posted February 26, 2026" (p1). Journal version also 2026.
venue: **Dual, and the split matters.** What is held and read is a **bioRxiv preprint**, "(which was not certified by peer review)" (p1). The manuscript itself states its destination: "it has been submitted exclusively to Cell Reports Physical Science" (p40). The published version is *Cell Reports Physical Science* 2026. Tagged `preprint` for what was actually read; the corpus should cite the journal version (see `unresolved`).
title: Decoding the Allosteric Paradox: A Dual Framework Integrating AI Cofolding Models with Landscape-Guided Interpretable AI Framework of Ligand-Protein Binding (p1). The journal version is understood to be retitled; the held PDF carries only this title.
system: **General protein**, with a protein-kinase sub-stratum. The orthosteric side spans "kinases, GPCRs, nuclear receptors, and ion channels" (MDT, p9) plus 76 Pfam families (PLOC, p33); the allosteric side is 353 protein-kinase complexes (KinCoRe Type III/IV + a curated X-ray set) plus 1,613 non-kinase structures across "83 Pfam families across >500 organisms" (PLA, p34). No per-family or per-system breakdown of results is ever reported — every number in the paper is pooled across all families.
n_targets: **Counted in complexes, never in distinct proteins.** Orthosteric: MDT 412 + PLOC 1,863 = **2,275 complexes** (2,325 binding pockets, 1,647 unique ligands) (p9, p33). Allosteric: KinCoRe 217 (Type III/IV) + curated X-ray 136 = 353 kinase, + PLA 1,613 non-kinase = **1,966 complexes** (1,830 pockets, 1,277 unique ligands) (p11, p34). **Combined n = 4,241 complexes.** The number of distinct *proteins* is NOT REPORTED on either side — which is exactly the number that would bear on redundancy and memorization. Figure 6 is visibly redundant at the protein level (4 of its 12 allosteric exemplars are PTP1B: 1BZC, 1NWE, 5KA1, 2VEV, p29).
method_class: **benchmark-only + other.** Two components: (i) a retrospective co-folding benchmark on stratified orthosteric/allosteric complexes; (ii) an interpretability layer of local frustration analysis (conformational and mutational frustration indices vs 1,000-decoy ensembles) run on experimental apo and holo structures, not on predictions (p36). No new predictor, no sampling method, no fine-tuning.
backbones: **Five, head to head: AF3, Protenix, Boltz-2, Chai-1, DynamicBind** (p6, p34). Tagged `multi-backbone`. A sixth arm is defined in Methods and never reported: "Predictions were generated with templates enabled (default) and without templates (AF3-NT)." (p34) — **no AF3-NT result appears anywhere in the paper.**
templates: **on** for AF3 ("templates enabled (default)", p34). For Protenix, Boltz-2, Chai-1 and DynamicBind the template setting is **NOT REPORTED** — the paper says only "All models received identical inputs: protein sequences from PDB structures, ligands in SMILES format." (p34), which describes inputs, not template retrieval. The declared AF3-NT (no-template) arm is the one place templates were to be controlled and its results are absent.
msa_handling: **NOT REPORTED.** The words MSA, alignment depth, subsampling and clustering do not appear in the Methods at all. The only sequence-signal statement is for Chai-1: "Predictions were made with the ESM embedding option enabled." (p35). Default MSA pipelines are therefore presumed but never stated, and no MSA manipulation of any kind (subsampling or state-filtering) was performed.
states_generated: **ensemble + single-state.** Per complex, 25 independent predictions were generated for AF3/Protenix/Boltz-2/Chai-1 ("10 recycling steps, 200 diffusion steps, 5 seeds, 5 diffusion samples per seed", p34) and 20 trajectories for DynamicBind (p35) — an ensemble. That ensemble is then collapsed to one: "For each model, the best prediction per complex (lowest ligand pose RMSD) was selected from generated models." (p37). Every headline number is a mean of these single best-of-25 values. Note the object is a **ligand-pose ensemble per complex**, not a protein conformational-state ensemble; the paper never targets, names or scores a protein conformational state.
structural_priors_used: Heavy, and entirely legitimate as *design*-time knowledge — it is what the benchmark is made of. (1) Every complex is a deposited experimental structure, used as the scoring reference (p33–34). (2) The orthosteric/allosteric stratification is taken wholesale from curated structural resources: the MDT set (ref 39), the PLOC/PLA subsets (ref 86), and **KinCoRe**, "a geometry-driven classification system using DFG motif and αC-helix conformation" from which "we extracted 217 Type III/IV complexes" (p34). (3) Allosteric membership is asserted structurally: "All complexes were experimentally validated as authentic allosteric binders with sites spatially distinct from orthosteric pockets." (p34). (4) MDT selection itself uses a structural prior: "Structural challenge was enforced by requiring AlphaFold-predicted apo-pocket deviation from experimental holo-conformation >2.0 Å RMSD or pocket LDDT <0.80." (p33). (5) The frustration analysis is computed on experimental apo and holo structures (p36), not on model output. None of this is a defect; it is recorded here so that `oracle_leakage` records only what entered the *pipeline*.
oracle_leakage: **All seven routes worked below. Verdict: pipeline leakage on routes 5 and 6 (explicit and severe), partial on route 1; design-level oracle on route 7.** See the per-route table immediately following this section.
prospective: **no.** Fully retrospective. Every complex has its experimental reference in hand before prediction; success, pocket definition, model selection and stratum membership are all defined against that reference. The authors nowhere claim prospectivity for their own work; the one use of the word is about someone else's study ("In a prospective evaluation of 557 SARS-CoV-2 Mac1-ligand complexes Kim et al. …", p32).
state_metric: **RMSD-to-reference + binary predicate**, with a third, unacknowledged **visual** component. (i) Continuous: symmetry-corrected ligand pose RMSD via OpenStructure SCRMSDScorer, "which enumerates symmetry-equivalent atom assignments and returns the lowest RMSD" (p35); pocket backbone RMSD after TM-align superposition, pocket = "all protein residues with at least one atom within 8 Å of any reference ligand atom" (p35–36); QS-score = "the fraction of native ligand–protein contacts (4.5 Å cutoff) correctly recovered" (p36). (ii) Binary: success at **RMSD < 2.0 Å** (p9, Fig 2D caption p11). The 2.0 Å threshold is adopted from PoseBusters convention and is **never independently justified** in this paper. The 8 Å pocket radius, the 4.5 Å contact cutoff and the 4 Å binding-site radius used for frustration (p37) are likewise stated without justification. (iii) Visual: the paper's spatial frustration claims — connected 8–12 Å minimal-frustration "shells" around orthosteric pockets vs "isolated, spatially disconnected patches" at allosteric sites (p25, p28) — are read off surface renders (Figs 5, 6) with **no contiguity metric, no cluster-size statistic and no quantitative panel of any kind**. Frustration *classes* are Z-score thresholded (minimal Z > 0.78, highly Z < −1.0, neutral in between, p36–37), but their *spatial organisation*, which is the load-bearing explanatory claim, is called by eye.
metric_saturation: **Yes, on QS-score, at the ceiling.** QS-score is bounded at 1.0 and the orthosteric arm sits against that bound: "QS-scores exceeding 0.90 across all models" and "AF3 and Protenix approaching 0.95" (p9, p17); Fig 3K/3O show orthosteric QS swarms centred at ~0.95 with essentially no headroom. The paper reads the modest allosteric shift (0.70–0.85) as a *decoupling* result — "models frequently identify the correct regulatory region … but fail to resolve these interactions into a unique geometric arrangement" (p17) — but a compressed metric near ceiling cannot distinguish that reading from insensitivity of the metric. Protenix is the clean case: Fig 3M shows orthosteric ≈ 0.93 and allosteric ≈ 0.92, i.e. no separation at all on QS. Success rate at 2.0 Å is a floor/ceiling-prone binary predicate by construction but is not reported at either bound. **No axis-truncation issue is recorded here** — Fig 3K–O truncation and Fig 2 axis handling are figure defects and live in `hides` on rows `3K-O` and `2A-B`.
directional_control: **None. The method is not instructable, and this is not a method paper.** The only conditioning handle is the ligand itself (protein sequence + ligand SMILES, p34) — the models are run in their stock configuration and asked to place a ligand. Diversity within a complex comes only from stochastic sampling ("5 seeds, 5 diffusion samples per seed", p34); no seed, subsample depth, template, partner, nanobody or state-annotated input is used to steer toward a state. DynamicBind is the one architecture with an explicit conformational handle ("iteratively adjusts receptor structure to accommodate the ligand", p35) and it is not directed either. No arm anywhere in the paper attempts to *instruct* a model to find an allosteric site.
anti_memorization_design: **Partial, asymmetric, and stated only for the orthosteric side.** In the **Orthosteric Datasets** section: "The datasets were filtered to include only complexes deposited in the Protein Data Bank after 2020, ensuring they post-date model training sets. Complexes with >30% sequence identity to training data were excluded (verified via PDB70 and MMseqs2 clustering)." (p33). Three problems. (a) **Scope**: the sentence sits between the MDT description and the PLOC description; "The datasets" is plural but it is unclear whether the 1,863-structure PLOC subset is covered. n for the filtered set is therefore either 412 or 2,275 and the paper does not say. (b) **Cutoff definition**: "after 2020" is not post-cutoff for the models tested — AF3's training set runs to late 2021 and Protenix, Boltz-2 and Chai-1 are later still. A 2020 date filter does not establish held-out status for any of the five architectures, and no model-specific cutoff date is given for any of them. (c) **The allosteric side has none.** The **Allosteric Datasets** section (p34) states resolution (≤3.5 Å, ≤3.2 Å), molecular weight (≥250 Da), inhibitor type (Type III/IV geometry) and site distinctness — **no deposition-date filter and no sequence-identity filter at all**. The stratum that carries the entire headline claim is the one with no memorization control.
anti_memorization_control: **NONE RUN.** No arm compares pre-cutoff to post-cutoff complexes, on either stratum. No arm compares high- to low-sequence-identity-to-training complexes. The asymmetry in (c) above is never named, never tested, and never discussed. This is the single largest gap between what the paper claims — "This uniformity across diverse inductive biases argues against explanations rooted in training data or architectural idiosyncrasies." (p30) — and what it measured: **a training-data explanation is precisely what was not controlled for on the allosteric arm**, and the direction of the confound is unexamined. (An unfiltered allosteric set would if anything make the observed failure *more* striking, but only if training overlap were quantified, which it is not.) Not marked `UNPOWERED`: n is large (1,966 allosteric complexes); the defect is design, not power.
confidence_as_discriminator: **Declared, used for ranking, contradicted, and never validated or reported.** Methods specify ligand-centric confidence metrics — "L-pLDDT (mean pLDDT over ligand atoms) and L-PAE (average PAE involving ligand atoms) for AF3/Chai-1, and ipTM for Boltz-2. Confidence-Error Correlation was assessed by mapping confidence scores against actual RMSD." (p36) — and a further "Spearman's rank correlation was computed between per-residue frustration Z-scores and per-residue model confidence scores." (p37). **No confidence result, correlation coefficient, calibration plot or panel appears anywhere in the paper.** Worse, the two selection statements contradict: "The ligand-protein chain-pair iPTM score was used for ranking." (p34) vs "For each model, the best prediction per complex (lowest ligand pose RMSD) was selected" (p37). Since the reported numbers are best-by-RMSD, confidence was **not** in fact the discriminator for anything reported. The one confidence claim in the Results is qualitative and unbacked: "the spatial extent of these networks correlates with prediction confidence" (p26, repeated in the Fig 5 caption p27) — asserted with no correlation statistic and no panel.
stance:
**`contrast` on rigour + `precedent` on findings** (provisional; the user's call).
*Precedent on findings*: this is the corpus's clearest large-n statement that current co-folding models have a site-class-dependent failure mode — five architectures, 4,241 complexes, a ~2× error gap that holds across all of them — together with a physical hypothesis (frustration neutrality) for why. If a manuscript argues that co-folding models collapse away from the canonical, memorised pocket, this is the citation for the phenomenon.
*Contrast on rigour*: the gap is measured between two oracle-selected best-of-25 values (route 6), on strata that are not matched for training-set overlap (only the orthosteric side carries a date/identity filter), with the one designed template control (AF3-NT) and all four declared statistical and confidence analyses unreported, and with several headline numbers contradicted by the paper's own figures. The architecture-independence claim in particular rests on five models that are not architecturally independent in the relevant sense (see `unresolved`).
n_predictions: **Samples per target:** 25 for AF3, Protenix, Boltz-2, Chai-1 — "For each complex, 25 independent predictions were generated (10 recycling steps, 200 diffusion steps, 5 seeds, 5 diffusion samples per seed) on NVIDIA A100 40GB GPUs." (p34); 20 for DynamicBind — "During inference, DynamicBind generates 20 candidate trajectories per target" (p35). **Targets:** 2,275 orthosteric + 1,966 allosteric = 4,241 complexes, each run through all five models. **Total:** never stated by the paper; arithmetic gives 4,241 × 25 × 4 + 4,241 × 20 ≈ **508,900 predictions**, plus an unreported AF3-NT arm if it was executed (a further ≈106,000). **Reported per complex: exactly 1** — the best-of-25 by RMSD (p37).
si_in_scope: **SI NOT HELD — and it holds all the per-model, per-complex detail.** Eight supplementary figures are cited in Results and none is in the 62-page PDF: S1 and S2 (per-prediction "bulb scatter plots" of RMSD against QS-score, orthosteric and allosteric — the panels that actually demonstrate the topology/geometry decoupling, p17–18); S3 (representative predicted-vs-experimental structure overlays, p18); S4 (granular sub-ångström distribution analysis, the source of the "72% of orthosteric complexes below 2.0 Å" figure, p18–19); S5–S8 (residue-level conformational and mutational frustration profiles for the orthosteric and allosteric representative panels, p26, p28). The paper asserts "The data supporting this article have also been included in the Supplementary Information." (p39). Underlying data and code are, however, deposited and public: Zenodo https://zenodo.org/records/18424406, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18424405, and GitHub https://github.com/Verkhivker-Research-Group/AI-CoFolding-Allostery-Benchmark (p38–39); structures are not archived and are re-downloaded from the RCSB PDB by the provided scripts (p39). Per-complex numbers are therefore recoverable from the repository but are absent from the document.

venue: **bioRxiv preprint. Explicitly not peer reviewed** — page header, p1: "this version posted June 18, 2025 … (which was not certified by peer review)". Tagged `preprint`.
title: Boltz-2: Towards Accurate and Efficient Binding Affinity Prediction — p1
system: **general protein** (and beyond protein: DNA, RNA, ligands, MHC-peptide, TCR-pMHC, antibody–antigen). Evaluation reaches into **protein kinases** specifically for affinity (FEP+ 4-target subset = CDK2, TYK2, JNK1, P38, p36; TYK2 prospective screen, p10–11; validation assays include ABL1/P00519, Q9Y5S2, O96013, p44) and into **GPCRs** as validation assay targets (P21453, P51686, P41146, P43115, Fig 12 p44) — but no conformational-state work on either family. p1 self-description: "a new structural biology foundation model".
n_targets: - Structure benchmark: **2315 unique targets** from PDB 01/01/24–12/31/2024 (p35). - MD benchmark: **40 complexes per dataset** for mdCATH and ATLAS test sets (p19). - Antibody benchmark: n **NOT REPORTED** (Fig 4 left, p8 — no n in caption or text). - Polaris-ASAP: n **NOT REPORTED** (top-10 competition entries shown, p8). - Affinity: OpenFE subset **876 protein–ligand complexes** (p36); focused subset **4 targets / 87 neutral compounds** (p36); CASP16 **140 protein–ligand pairs across two targets** (p9); MF-PCBA **10 HTS assays**, each downsampled to 50,000 complexes (p36); private Recursion **8 blinded hit-to-lead assays** (p10, p43); hit-to-lead validation set **16 assays** (p36). - Prospective screen: **1 target (TYK2)**, p10. - Training targets: ~**2k** protein clusters at 90% identity for ChEMBL/BindingDB affinity data, plus 300 (PubChem HTS), 1.3k (CeMM), 60 (MIDAS), 250 (PubChem small assays) — Table 1, p4.
method_class: **co-folding** (diffusion-based all-atom structure prediction) **+ affinity prediction head + inference-time physics steering**. Also trained on MD trajectories and benchmarked against MD emulators. Not MSA-subsampling, not clustering, not enhanced sampling.
backbones: **Boltz-2** (this work), compared head to head against **AlphaFold3, Chai-1, ProteinX, Boltz-1, Boltz-1x, Boltz-2x** on the PDB benchmark (Fig 3, p7; baselines p35: "For all tools, we use the same inference parameters (5 recycling rounds, 5 samples, single seed) and the same MSA"). MD baselines: **Boltz-1, AlphaFlow-MD base, BioEmu** (p36). Five distinct backbones compared → tagged `multi-backbone`.
templates: **supported but OFF in every evaluation reported.** p35, PDB baselines: "We do not use templates during evaluation." Template conditioning and template steering are described (p24) but p40 states their evaluation is not yet in the paper. During *training* templates are used: "We produce template hits for protein chains as described in AlphaFold3, using hmmbuild and hmmsearch on PDB sequences deposited at least 60 days prior to any given query's deposition date" (p16); sampling: 60% of the time no templates, otherwise 1–4 from the top-20 hits (p28).
msa_handling: **full, with randomised sampling and 5% full dropout at training time.** p28: "at training time, we do not select MSA sequences greedily, but we rather sample them randomly among the top 16k hits… we aim at improving the model performance in this setting by randomly dropping all of the MSA of a complex in 5% of training iterations." Max 8192 MSA sequences during training (Table 6, p29). MSAs computed with ColabFold search, taxonomy-paired via Uniref100 (p16). At inference, all baselines "were run with the same MSA and sequence inputs" (p36). **This is not subsampling as a state handle and not state-filtering** — it is training-time regularisation. ---
states_generated: **ensemble + single-state.** - *Ensemble* arm: with MD method conditioning the model produces diverse ensembles — p7: "(1) MD conditioning has a clear effect on the predicted ensembles, leading to more diverse structures that better capture the conformational diversity of the simulations". MD evaluation used **100 samples** per target against 200 reference frames (p35). Trained on ensembles: p3 — "Unlike Boltz-1, which trained on a single structure per system, we supervise Boltz-2 using ensembles coming from both experimental techniques, such as NMR, as well as computational ones, such as molecular dynamics." - *Single-state* arm and default: the reported structure is top-1 of 5 — p35: "For each result, we provide the top-1 prediction across 5 samples according to the confidence model ranking." The affinity module consumes "the top-ranked structure from five samples generated over 200 diffusion steps each, ranked according to their protein-ligand ipTM-score" (p26). - **No conformational-state capability is claimed, and the opposite is stated.** p12, Limitations: "the model still often fails to capture large conformational changes, such as those that can be induced by binding." The diversity achieved is *local* fluctuation / RMSF-scale, and even there is bettered by the specialists — p8: "This diversity increase is, however, outperformed by BioEmu and AlphaFlow, which more closely align with the reference diversity from the simulation." - **structural_priors_used** (design-time deposited knowledge; not a defect): 1. **The entire PDB up to 2023-06-01** as structural training data (p16), plus B-factors extracted from PDB entries (p16). 2. **AFDB / AlphaFold2 predictions** — ~5 million monomers, filtered at global lDDT ≥ 0.5 (p18); 0.380 sampling weight, the second largest single source (Table 2, p18). 3. **Boltz-1 self-distillation** across RNA, protein-DNA, RNA-ligand, protein-ligand, TCR-pMHC, MHC-I, MHC-II (p17–18). 4. **MD trajectories** from MISATO (11,235 systems), ATLAS (1,284 proteins), mdCATH (5,270 systems) — p16–17. All three are seeded from deposited PDB entries: p19 — "all entries from the MD datasets correspond to PDB structures released before the validation cutoff date of 2023-06-01". 5. **TYK2 protein-ligand complexes from the PDB were in the structure-module training data** — p49, stated by the authors: "The Boltz-2 structure module was trained using TYK2 protein-ligand complexes from the PDB." 6. **KLIFS** used post hoc only, to assess novelty of generated ligands — p49: "we collected the 47 public TYK2 inhibitors from the KLIFS database … that correspond to the co-crystalized TYK2 inhibitors from the PDB." Not used to bias any prediction. 7. **Deliberate upsampling of SARS-CoV-2 Mpro-like proteins in training** — p18: "we upsample interfaces containing antibodies and TCR, as these are specific modalities that we wanted the model to improve on, as well as proteins similar to SARS-CoV2-Mpro **as we had planned to participate in the Polaris-ASAP competition**" (weight 0.015, Table 2 p18). Recorded here as a design-time choice; its consequence for the reported Polaris-ASAP result is in `oracle_leakage` routes 4 and 7.
oracle_leakage: seven routes, each answered separately. **Route 1 — deposited structures used as input or template.** **NONE FOUND for the reported evaluations.** p35 (protocol page): "For all tools, we use the same inference parameters (5 recycling rounds, 5 samples, single seed) and the same MSA. **We do not use templates during evaluation.**" The affinity module takes *predicted* structures, not deposited ones: p31 — "For each protein–ligand complex, we run Boltz-2 structure model with 5 recycling iterations, 200 diffusion steps, and generate 5 candidate structures." One partial exception, in a *baseline*, not in Boltz-2: p39 — "In the absense of experimental crystal structures in MF-PCBA, we co-fold the median-weight active compound of each assay with Boltz-2 to obtain the receptor structure for Docking." **Route 2 — state annotations from a curated database (GPCRdb / KLIFS / Kincore) driving templates or alignments.** **NONE FOUND.** KLIFS appears exactly once and only post hoc, p49 (quoted under `structural_priors_used` item 6); it drives a Tanimoto novelty analysis of generated ligands, not any prediction. No GPCRdb, no Kincore, no state annotation anywhere. **Route 3 — cluster labels derived from known states.** **NONE FOUND.** All clustering in the paper is by *sequence identity*, never by state: p18 — "mmseqs easy-cluster … –min-seq-id 0.4" for structural splits; p37 — "clustering all protein sequences in the affinity datasets using 'mmseqs easy-cluster … –min-seq-id 0.9 –cov-mode 0 -c 0.01'". Ligand clustering is by Tanimoto similarity (p19, p22). **Route 4 — hyperparameters, sweep ranges, seeds or stopping criteria tuned against the evaluation set.** **THREE FINDINGS, all admitted by the authors.** (a) *Calibration constants fitted on a validation set drawn from the training corpus.* p27: "we apply a calibrated ensembling strategy. We first compute the mean predicted affinity between models and then apply a molecular weight correction of the form ŷ = C0·(y1+y2) + C1·MW_binder + C2, where … C0, C1, and C2 are **fitted in the holdout validation set**". And that validation set is itself drawn from training data: p36 — "we curate a validation set by **selecting a diverse collection of hit-to-lead assays from our training corpus**." This is validation-set tuning, not test-set tuning, and the test sets are separately protected (see `anti_memorization_design`) — but it is a fitted post-hoc correction applied to every reported affinity number. (b) *Steering hyperparameters tuned; tuning set never stated.* p23: "Boltz-2 adopts the steering potentials we proposed in Boltz-1x **with tuned hyperparameters** and a normalization of each potential by the number of elements on which they are applied." What they were tuned against is not given anywhere in the paper. (c) *Training-data composition chosen with a benchmark in view.* p18: "…as well as proteins similar to SARS-CoV2-Mpro **as we had planned to participate in the Polaris-ASAP competition**", and the Polaris-ASAP result is then reported retrospectively as a headline (p7, Fig 4 right). No sweep or per-target tuning is involved, so this is training-set enrichment against a named evaluation rather than pipeline leakage; it is labelled design-level (route 7) below. For completeness, the paper flags the same class of problem in a *baseline*: p39 — "the results of the ABFE protocol [Wu et al., 2025] on the 4 target subset **may also represent an optimistic estimate of its prospective performance given that the protocol was optimized based this dataset**", and p39 on FEP+ — "The results of FEP+ are intended to show the maximum attainable accuracy of current (commercial) FEP simulations **by manually adjusting the protocol (input preparation, perturbation map, force field) to the system at hand after observing the error with respect to the experiment**." **Route 5 — success defined post hoc by RMSD/TM to a structure they held.** **PRESENT, and standard for a retrospective structure benchmark; absent for the prospective screen, where a different oracle substitutes.** Structure benchmarks score lDDT and DockQ against deposited references (p35, "The lDDT … DockQ which we use to score antibody interfaces"), which is retrospective scoring against a held reference by construction. For the prospective TYK2 screen there is **no experimental readout at all**; success is defined by a simulation the authors also wrote — p10: "in the absence of experimental data, we validate the compounds selected by Boltz-2 with a single repeat of Boltz-ABFE, our recently developed absolute FEP pipeline". The authors flag the resulting circularity themselves, p11: "We note that these results might be optimistic given that Boltz-2 performs well on this target based on the protein-ligand benchmark data [Hahn et al., 2022], achieving Pearson R = 0.83." **Route 6 — best/worst model labels assigned against a held reference.** **NONE FOUND.** Ranking among samples is by the model's own confidence, never by the reference. p35: "For each result, we provide the top-1 prediction across 5 samples **according to the confidence model ranking**." p26: "the top-ranked structure from five samples … **ranked according to their protein-ligand ipTM-score**." p30: "We select the most confident structure according to the inter-chain predicted TM-score (ipTM)." **Route 7 — design-level oracle use (weaker than pipeline leakage; label kept distinct).** **PRESENT, twice, both stated openly by the authors.** (a) *The prospective target was chosen because the validator is known to work on it.* p10: "We selected TYK2 for two main reasons: First, TYK2 is in the test set of the Boltz-2 affinity model, avoiding data leakage from known binders. Second, in the absence of experimental data, we validate the compounds selected by Boltz-2 with a single repeat of Boltz-ABFE … **and Boltz-ABFE performs very well on this target**. Indeed, based on the protein-ligand benchmark, Boltz-ABFE achieves a Pearson R = 0.95, centered MAE = 0.42 kcal/mol … supporting our confidence of this procedure as a validation step for TYK2-targeting virtual screens." The first reason is a genuine anti-leakage measure; the second is target selection conditioned on the oracle's known performance. (b) *Training data enriched for a benchmark family before entering that benchmark* — the SARS-CoV-2 Mpro upsampling quoted at route 4(c), p18, with the Polaris-ASAP result reported at p7 and Fig 4 right, p8. **Summary line:** pipeline routes 1, 2, 3 and 6 are clean and the protocol pages that establish that are p35–p37; the real findings are route 4 (a fitted molecular-weight calibration on a validation set carved out of the training corpus, and untraceable steering-hyperparameter tuning) and route 7 (target and training composition chosen with the answer's difficulty already known). Route 5 is retrospective-by-design for structures and is replaced by a self-authored simulation oracle for the one prospective experiment.
prospective: **partial.** - *Prospective:* the TYK2 virtual screen (460,160 HLL + 64,960 Kinase library + 117,199 SynFlowNet-generated compounds scored, p11, p46 Table 17) selects compounds with no known answer, and CASP16 is a genuine blind challenge run out of the box — p9: "we ran Boltz-2 out-of-the-box with no fine-tuning or input curation", and p37: "CASP16 data was released after our training data cutoff". The 8 Recursion assays are described as "blinded" (p10, p43). - *Retrospective:* everything else. The PDB, antibody, MD, FEP+, OpenFE, MF-PCBA benchmarks are all retrospective; Polaris-ASAP is explicitly "Retrospective results for the Polaris-ASAP competition" (Fig 4 caption, p8). - *Why not fully prospective:* the one prospective arm has no experimental readout (route 5) and its target was chosen for oracle convenience (route 7a).
state_metric: **continuous coordinate + binary predicate.** Dual, and both halves are used for headline claims. - Continuous: lDDT per modality and per interface (p35); Pearson r / Spearman ρ / RMSE on RMSF (p35); Pearson R, Kendall τ, PMAE, MAE for affinity (p37); AP, AUROC, global AUROC (p38). - Binary predicates with **explicit but unjustified thresholds**: **DockQ > 0.23** and **DockQ > 0.49** for antibody interfaces (Fig 3 p7, Fig 4 p8) — thresholds shown on the axis, never justified in text; **< 2 Å** ligand-pose success for Polaris-ASAP (Fig 4 right, p8) — threshold in the axis label only; **Perc. within 1 and 2 kcal/mol** (p38, defined but the choice of 1 and 2 kcal/mol is not justified); **Enrichment Factor at 0.5/1/2/5%** (p38); **ABFE binding region < −5.45 kcal/mol** (Fig 8 legend, p11) — the threshold that converts every "predicted to bind" statement on p11 into a count, and **its derivation is NOT REPORTED anywhere in the paper**. - **No conformational-state predicate of any kind exists in this paper.** No active/inactive call, no RMSD-to-alternate-state, no state label.
metric_saturation: **YES, numerically, in the affinity tables.** "Perc. within 2 kcal/mol" ceilings at 1.00 for two methods on the 4-target FEP subset — FEP+ non-centered/centered = 1.00, and BACPI centered = 1.00, with Boltz-2 at 0.97/0.98 and OpenFE at 0.98 (Table 12, p42): the metric cannot separate the best from the worst method there. Per-assay panels hit the same
directional_control: **YES for geometry and experimental modality; NO for conformational state.** Handles named by the paper, all inference-time: 1. **Experimental-method conditioning** — a one-hot method token: p24, "at training time, we condition the model to the experimental method … At inference time, users can decide on which experimental method to use to condition the model's prediction." Methods listed p24: "X-ray diffraction, electron microscopy, solution NMR, solid-state NMR, molecular dynamics, distillation from AlphaFold2 and distillation from Boltz-1." This is the **only handle with a demonstrated effect on the output distribution** (Fig 5 p8; Tables 9–10 p40: Boltz-2-MD vs Boltz-2-Xray, global RMSF r 0.67 vs 0.48 on mdCATH, 0.65 vs 0.57 on ATLAS). It selects *ensemble breadth and B-factor character*, not a named conformational state. 2. **Multimeric template conditioning + template steering** — p24: "we allow for multimeric templates and we allow the user to strictly enforce that templates are respected via a Boltz-steering potential", pushing template atoms "to have a structure within α_cutoff Å of the given template". **Not evaluated in this version (p40).** 3. **Contact and pocket conditioning + steering** — p25, distance constraints "constrained to be 4Å ≤ d ≤ 20Å", fed as pairwise features and additionally enforced by a steering potential. **Not evaluated in this version (p40).** 4. **Seeds** — "single seed" at evaluation (p35); diffusion multiplicity 32 at training (Table 6, p29). Not offered as a control handle. - **No state-annotated template, no state-filtered MSA, no state label input exists.** In principle a user could supply a state-specific template and enforce it via template steering, but the paper never frames, tests or claims this.
anti_memorization_design: **PRESENT and multi-layered. This is the authoritative record of the Boltz-2 cutoff.** **THE TRAINING CUTOFF, VERBATIM:** > "We use every PDB structure up to the **training date cutoff of 06/01/2023**." — **p16** (Appendix A.1.1, first bullet). Restated twice more, in ISO form: > "The experimental data used for training comprises structures in the Protein Data Bank (PDB) > [Berman et al., 2000] **released before 2023-06-01**." — **p3** (§2, Structural Data). > "Given that all entries from the MD datasets correspond to PDB structures released before the > **validation cutoff date of 2023-06-01** …" — **p19** (A.1.5). Held-out sets built against it: - **Validation set, n = 398 PDB structures** — p19: "Initial release date is before 2023-06-01 (exclusive) and 2024-01-01 (inclusive)", resolution < 4.5 Å, all protein sequences absent from every training cluster (mmseqs at 0.4 identity), plus a ligand-novelty condition ("At least one of the small-molecules exhibits a Tanimoto similarity of 0.85 or less to any small-molecule in the training set"). "This results in a total of 398 structures from PDB in our validation set." - **Structure test set, n = 2315 unique targets** — p35: "recently released structures from the PDB, specifically from **01/01/24 to 12/31/2024**.
