title: KinConfBench: A Curated Benchmark for Cofolding Models on Kinase Conformational States — p1
system: **protein kinase** — human protein kinase catalytic domains exclusively. p3: "we introduce KinConfBench, a curated benchmark of 2,225 high-quality human kinase chains". Only catalytically competent kinase domains; pseudokinase domains are explicitly removed (p4: "we use the reference sequences of the active kinase domains extracted from UniProt to selectively retain only the catalytic units while excluding pseudokinase domains"). No GPCRs, transporters or non-kinase systems anywhere.
n_targets: multi-level; record all four, because a single number misrepresents the scale: - **437** catalytically active human kinase domains seed the query (p3, following Faezov & Dunbrack [34]). - **2,225** structurally unique kinase chains in the final benchmark (p4–p5): 236 unique apo chains + 1,989 unique holo chains. - **1,420** unique kinase *systems* actually run through inference (p3, p13): "43 unique apo targets and 1,377 unique holo complexes". - **Analysis subsets are much smaller and are conditioned on model success:** 950 systems pass the geometric filter for the KinCoRe-correctness analysis (p6); 509 systems form the ensemble-diversity subset (p9); **234** holo/apo pairs enter the apo-drift analysis, split per model into train/test as 212/22 (Boltz-2), 182/52 (Chai-1), 194/40 (Protenix) (p11 Figure 5 caption). - **Generality flag:** the paper's conclusions are framed for cofolding models and SBDD in general ("critical for next-generation structure-based drug discovery", p1) but rest entirely on one protein family. The authors state this scoping themselves (p12).
method_class: **benchmark-only.** The paper builds and curates a benchmark dataset and evaluates three existing cofolding models; it proposes no new predictor and modifies no inference pipeline. p12–13: "we adhere to the official inference pipelines for each method to represent standard usage scenarios."
backbones: **Boltz-2 [15], Chai-1 [13], Protenix [16]** — three open-source cofolding models compared head to head on identical inputs (p3, p6, p13). **Tag `multi-backbone`.** No AF2, AF3, Chai-2, OpenFold or NeuralPLexer inference is run; AF3 and NeuralPLexer appear only as citations, and AF2 only via Faezov & Dunbrack's precomputed 437-domain set used for *target selection*, not for prediction.
templates: **NOT REPORTED.** The word "template" appears in the paper only in the biological sense ("common templates of the global fold", p3). Methods (p12–13) state MSA handling and sample count but never say whether each model's structural template channel was on, off, or left at repository default. Since the stated protocol is "we adhere to the official inference pipelines for each method", the setting is whatever each repository defaults to, which is not stated. Do not infer. Consequence: no protocol tag is applied.
msa_handling: **full, default per model.** p12–13: "Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSAs) are generated and cached with each tool's default databases and pairing strategies. For Boltz-2, Chai-1, and Protenix, the ColabFold server [3] is used for MSA generation, while sequence pairing follows the defaults of the respective model repositories." **No subsampling and no state-filtering** — this is the unmodified default-depth regime, which is what makes it a clean benchmark of stock model behaviour rather than a biasing study. Input sequences are trimmed: "Input sequences are restricted to the canonical kinase domain boundaries defined by UniProt, so that the benchmark stresses domain-level cofolding behavior" (p12–13).
states_generated: **ensemble + single-state.** This is the dual case the v3 field exists for, and the collapse is the paper's actual result. - *Ensemble* by construction: "To ensure robust sampling of the conformational landscape, we generate N = 20 cofolding samples per target for each inference run" (p13). - *Single-state* in outcome, on two independent measurements: - **Mode collapse across the ensemble** (p7): "Figure 2(c) shows that, despite the increase in accuracy, the co-folding model predictions are largely bimodal. This mostly all-right or all-wrong pattern suggests ensemble mode collapse rather than graded uncertainty within the twenty samples." Figure 2c shows >500 of 950 systems in the 20/20 bin and ~175 in the 0/20 bin for Boltz-2 and Protenix (p7). - **Negligible intra-basin diversity** (p9): "all models produce very small structural deviations of ∼0.1 Å for the distance metrics and less than 5° average angle exploration except for Chai-1's performance on Asp χ2", against a stated reference scale of "root mean square fluctuations of ∼1-2 Å and backbone or side chain dihedral angle ranges of 5° to 30°" for ordinary thermal fluctuation (p9–10). - Note the structures are generated by the three evaluated models, not by a method of the authors' own; the authors ran the inferences (p13).
structural_priors_used: **Heavy, and entirely legitimate for a benchmark — this is where the deposited-structure dependence belongs, not in `oracle_leakage`.** 1. **The Modi–Dunbrack kinase nomenclature** as the state ontology: p3, "we employ the structural nomenclature developed by Modi and Dunbrack [31], labeling kinase chains with categorical structural features to capture specific active and inactive conformations." Eight categorical labels (spatial/DFG, dihedral/X-DFG, helix/αC, salt bridge, N- and C-terminal activation loop, spine, activity), enumerated p3–4. 2. **The KinCoRe / Kincore software suite** [35, 36] as the classifier: p3, "we process all chains from the identified entries using the KinCoRe software suite [35, 36]." 3. **Faezov & Dunbrack's 437 catalytically competent human kinase domains** [34] as the target list: p3, "we first identify 437 catalytically active human kinase domains and their corresponding UniProt [33] identifiers, following the classification established by Faezov and Dunbrack [34]." 4. **The PDB itself** as the entire universe of systems: p3, RCSB "(snapshot 2025-08-01)", 7,763 raw entries. 5. **UniProt canonical kinase domain boundaries** define the input sequence (p12–13). 6. **The 12 experimentally observed KinCoRe label combinations** as the space of allowed answers: p6, "KinCoRe assigns each kinase protein structure to valid spatial and dihedral label combinations (36 theoretical, 12 observed in the PDB; Supplementary Table S1)".
oracle_leakage: **Present, but entirely on the EVALUATION and SELECTION side, not on the input side.** No knowledge of the target state reaches the models: their input is the kinase domain sequence plus the ligand SMILES, with a default full MSA and no state-annotated template (p12–13). Route-by-route: - **Route 1 — structures used as input or template: NONE FOUND at the benchmark level, with one gap.** The protocol is described p12–13; input is sequence + ligand only, per the abstract (p1): "cofolding models can generate global folds directly from kinase sequences and ligand SMILES strings". No experimental structure is fed to any model. *Gap:* whether each repository's default enables a PDB template search is never stated (see `templates`), so route 1 cannot be closed with full confidence from this PDF. Also note every reference structure is in the PDB and the models were trained on the PDB — training-set memorization is the paper's own subject matter, not a protocol leak (p10). - **Route 2 — state annotations from a curated database (Kincore) driving templates or alignments: NONE FOUND as a pipeline driver; PRESENT as the ground-truth definition.** KinCoRe is run on the *outputs*, never on the inputs. p6: "By applying the KinCoRe labels to every prediction, we establish a 'ground truth' based on the categorical orientation of the DFG motif and the αC-helix, providing a more functionally relevant metric than standard backbone RMSD." p13: "Post-inference, structures are passed through the Dunbrack KinCoRe annotation pipeline". The reference labels come from running the same classifier over the **deposited** chains (p3: "To assign conformational labels to the selected kinase PDB entries, we process all chains from the identified entries using the KinCoRe software suite"). So the database supplies the scoring function, symmetrically applied to prediction and to deposited reference, and never conditions the model. This is the single most important distinction in the note. - **Route 3 — cluster labels derived from known states: PRESENT, at dataset construction.** The benchmark's de-duplication and its retention of "meaningful structural diversity" are driven by the KinCoRe labels of deposited structures. p4: "we remove trivial redundancies, defined as entries sharing identical sequences (and ligand SMILES, where applicable) alongside identical KinCoRe conformational labels. Nevertheless, we preserve meaningful structural diversity by retaining any entry that exhibited at least one unique KinCoRe label relative to others of the same condition." The evaluation set is therefore shaped by the answer key; the model is not. - **Route 4 — hyperparameters, sweep ranges, seeds or stopping criteria tuned against known states: PARTIALLY PRESENT.** - *Not tuned:* the geometric thresholds are borrowed, not fitted. p6: "We define a geometrically successful prediction as one with global fold lDDT-Cα ≥ 0.7, binding pocket lDDT-PLI ≥ 0.8, and ligand RMSD < 2.0Å following the definition of previous works [2, 17]." N = 20 is fixed for all targets and all models (p13). - *Tuned on the evaluation outcome:* the diversity-subset cut is chosen so the models come out comparable. p9: "we focus on the 509 systems where Boltz-2, Chai-1, and Protenix each have at least ten all-correct structures according to KinCoRe in the top-20, so every cofolding method contributes a comparably populated success set based on classification." The "at least ten" threshold is set against results already computed on the evaluation set. Under the v3 clarification (tuning a *range* on the evaluation set is leakage even with no per-target value), this counts. - **Route 5 — success defined post hoc by RMSD/lDDT to a structure they had: PRESENT and load-bearing.** Both success definitions are defined against the held deposited structure, and the analysis set itself is conditioned on model success. p6: "Out of 1420 protein- ligand kinase systems, geometric filtering resulted in only 950 kinase where all cofolding models produce at least one geometrically valid pose out of 20 samples for downstream analysis." And p6: "a prediction is only considered 'correct' if all eight KinCoRe labels match those of the experimental structures." A softening clause is applied in the same direction (p7 caption): "we consider a prediction successful if it matches any valid set of ground truth labels associated with that protein-ligand complex." This is inherent to any retrospective benchmark and is not concealed, but it is route 5 and must be recorded. - **Route 6 — best/worst model labels assigned against a held reference: PRESENT.** The hard case and the failure list are both defined by disagreement with the reference. p8: "Supplementary Table 4 contains the 110 kinases where all three cofolding models fail to generate the correct conformation" and "Figure 3 highlights MAP4K1/YK1 (PDB ID: 7M0M) [42] as a representative hard case where all cofolding model predictions fail to obtain an induced-fit to the correct conformational state." Which of the 20 samples per model is the "representative" one rendered in Figure 3 is **NOT REPORTED** (p8 caption says only "representative Boltz-2 (green), Chai-1 (orange), and Protenix (blue) predictions"). - **Route 7 — design-level oracle use (systems or conditions chosen because the answer is already known): PRESENT and explicit, and this is the strongest design-level statement in the paper.** p10: "We extract kinase systems from KinConfBench that possess resolved structures for both states, restricting our analysis to systems where the ligand induces a distinct structural change defined as a different set of KinCoRe functional labels compared to ligand-free structures." Every apo-drift system is one where the correct holo answer and the wrong apo answer are both already deposited and already labelled. Weaker than pipeline leakage, and correct practice for a benchmark, but it must be labelled as design-level. **Verdict in one line:** model inputs are clean (sequence + SMILES, default full MSA, no state-annotated template, no state-filtered alignment), and every oracle route that fires — 3, 4 (partly), 5, 6, 7 — fires on the evaluation, selection or presentation side, which is what a retrospective benchmark is; route 2's Kincore dependence is a *scoring function* symmetrically applied to prediction and deposited reference, not a pipeline driver.
prospective: **no.** Fully retrospective. Every target is a deposited PDB entry from a 2025-08-01 snapshot (p3); every reference state, apo and holo, was solved before the analysis; success is defined by match to the deposited answer (p6). The apo-drift test set is *post-training-cutoff for the models* but not prospective for the authors — the structures already existed when the benchmark was built (see `anti_memorization_design`). No prediction is made about an unsolved system and no experiment is run.
state_metric: **binary predicate + continuous coordinate** (with RMSD-to-reference used as a pre-filter, not as the state call). - *Binary predicate (primary):* exact 8-of-8 categorical label match. p6: "a prediction is only considered 'correct' if all eight KinCoRe labels match those of the experimental structures." Relaxed to any-of-set where an entry carries multiple valid label sets (p7 caption). No threshold to state — it is a categorical identity test. - *Continuous coordinate (secondary, diversity only):* p8–9, "we extend our analysis beyond discrete accuracy to measure the structural dispersion within ensembles ... on a continuous scale for distances and dihedral angles as described in Supplementary Information." Twelve descriptors: Lys–Glu distance, salt bridge distance, spine distance, DFG–HRD distance, and Asp/Phe φ, ψ, χ1, χ2 (Figure 4, p9). Measured as within-ensemble standard deviation. Interpretive reference scale is stated but not used as a threshold: "root mean square fluctuations of ∼1-2 Å and backbone or side chain dihedral angle ranges of 5° to 30° define the statistical fluctuations of stable protein conformations [43, 44]" (p10). - *RMSD/lDDT-to-reference (pre-filter):* lDDT-Cα ≥ 0.7, lDDT-PLI ≥ 0.8, ligand heavy-atom RMSD < 2.0 Å, justification "following the definition of previous works [2, 17]" (p6). **The paper's central negative claim is precisely that this metric family does not determine the state call** — p1: "geometric success metrics of a ligand pose in the active site does not correlate strongly with the correct kinase conformational state". - *Not visual:* Figure 3 is a superposition, but the failure it illustrates is called by the KinCoRe predicate, not by eye. Do not tag `visual-metric`.
metric_saturation: **YES — numeric, in three arms.** 1. **All three geometric metrics are censored at their filter thresholds by construction.** Only predictions passing lDDT-Cα ≥ 0.7, lDDT-PLI ≥ 0.8 and ligand RMSD < 2.0 Å enter Figure 2a (p6), so the plotted distributions floor at 0.7 and 0.8 and ceiling at 2.0 Å. In Figure 2a (p7) the ligand-RMSD outlier mass piles into an unresolvable band against the 2.0 Å boundary in all nine sub-panels, and the lDDT-PLI boxes sit against 0.8. The metric cannot separate correct from incorrect below/above the cut because that region was removed. Cross-reference the `hides` entry for figure row 2A, which is the axis-pinning half of the same problem. 2. **The top-20 correctness count ceilings at 20** (Figure 2c, p7). >500 of 950 systems fall in the 20/20 bin for Boltz-2 and ~475 for Protenix; the metric cannot express "more reliably correct than 20 out of 20", so between-model differences at the top are compressed. The paper reads this saturation as the *result* (mode collapse), which is a defensible use, but the ceiling is real. 3. **The Top-K success curve is near-plateau within the sampled range** (Figure 2b, p7): all three curves are visually flat from K ≈ 10 to K = 20, so the K = 20 endpoint approximates the asymptote for these models rather than a still-rising value.
directional_control: **NONE — sampling only.** No handle exists in this study by which a model can be instructed which kinase state to produce. The only conditioning input is the **ligand SMILES** (p1: "directly from kinase sequences and ligand SMILES strings"), and the paper's finding is that this handle largely fails to steer the state: p10, models "effectively 'drift[] back' to the unperturbed, default apo state." The only ensemble handle exercised is repeated sampling, N = 20 per target (p13). No seed sweep, no MSA depth sweep, no state-annotated template, no partner, nanobody, peptide or G-protein mimetic. Ranking within the ensemble uses pLDDT (p7 caption), which is a selection handle, not a directional one.
anti_memorization_design: **YES — a per-model, deposition-date time split, with the cutoff stated explicitly for each model.** p10: "For each cofolding model, we define training and test sets based on a time split relevant to each model: a holo ligand combination counts as part of the test set if it first appears in the PDB only after that method's training-data deposition cutoff: Boltz-2 (2023-06-01); Chai-1 (2021-01-12); Protenix (2021-09-30))." - **n (test / train systems), from the Figure 5 caption, p11:** Boltz-2 **22** test / 212 train; Chai-1 **52** / 182; Protenix **40** / 194. Each model sees the same 234 holo/apo pairs, split differently because the cutoffs differ. - **Eligibility rule for the pair set** (p10): only systems with resolved apo *and* holo structures whose KinCoRe labels differ — i.e. only systems where a real induced-fit shift is documented. - **Critical asymmetry, stated by the authors** (p10): "All apo-state structures are found in the training data for all cofolding models." Only the holo half of each pair is ever held out. - Note there is **no held-out split anywhere else in the paper** — the 950-system correctness analysis (p6) and the 509-system diversity analysis (p9) use all deposited data with no date filter, so all Figure 2 and Figure 4 numbers are in-distribution for at least some of the models.
anti_memorization_control: **CONTROL ARM ACTUALLY RUN AND ANALYSED — one of the few papers in the corpus where this is true — but mark `UNPOWERED` on the overlap clause.** - *Run:* Figure 5 (p11) reports the four-way outcome distribution separately for the train split and the test split, per model, and the text compares them: p11, "when comparing to the test set distribution in Figure 5b against the training set, the stacked profiles further shift toward Apo-only and Dual-Match segments relative to the training systems—most clearly for Boltz-2 and Protenix—consistent with apo-drift when confronted with new holo states unsupported in the training statistics." Restated in the Discussion, p12: "After the training cutoff (specific to each model), we find that the holo state prediction rates fall and apo drift rises for each architecture." This is a genuine control arm, not a held-out set left unused. - *`UNPOWERED`, on the v3 overlap clause:* the held-out set overlaps training by explicit statement — "All apo-state structures are found in the training data for all cofolding models" (p10) — so each test pair is half in-training. On the n clause the arm passes (22 / 52 / 40 all exceed ~10), though Boltz-2's n = 22 means one system moves a stacked bar by ~4.5 percentage points, and the model on which the effect is called "most clearly" visible is the one with the smallest test n. - *No inferential statistic:* no test, confidence interval or error bar accompanies the train-vs-test comparison anywhere in the text or in Figure 5. The claim is read off the stack heights.
confidence_as_discriminator: **YES, used — and explicitly found wanting; the negative result is one of the paper's headline findings.** - *Used:* pLDDT ranks the ensemble for every Top-K number. p7 caption: "For each target, we evaluate an ensemble of N = 20 generated structures, ranked by their pLDDT confidence scores." - *Found wanting:* p3, "The resulting metrics show that high confidence in the active site geometry does not ensure high confidence in predicting the kinase conformational states, especially when ligands perturb the kinase away from common templates of the global fold." p11: "Framing success purely through the highest-confidence structure therefore obscures a clinically relevant failure mode: models can 'look' bound while adopting the wrong regulatory layout for the ligand at hand." The 11–13 pp Top-1→Top-20 gain (p7) is the quantitative form: the confidence ranking puts a wrong-state structure first in >11% of systems where a right-state structure exists in the ensemble. - *Validated as a use?* Yes, in the negative sense that matters: the ranking's discriminative power is measured against the KinCoRe ground truth rather than assumed. The prescription follows, p12: "Closing this gap likely demands both better generative breadth for rare induced-fit basins and confidence objectives that reward state discrimination, not only ligand-protein pocket aligned metrics."
stance: **`precedent` on findings + `background` on framing.** Provisional — the user's call, not settled here. - *Precedent on findings:* this paper independently documents, on 2,225 kinase chains and three backbones, the exact failure triad a conformational-control method exists to fix — mode collapse across a 20-member ensemble, within-basin dispersion an order of magnitude below thermal, and memorization-driven reversion to the apo state on post-cutoff holo complexes. It supplies the negative baseline rather than competing for the same result. - *Background on framing:* it is benchmark-only. It proposes no method, exercises no directional handle, and offers no state-control mechanism, so it cannot be a `threat`; it defines the problem statement and hands over a public dataset and a 110-system joint-failure list. - *Not `contrast`:* the paper's rigour is not the weak point one would argue against — its inputs are clean, its control arms are numerous and its limits are stated. The arguable rigour gaps (test n, apo-in-training, success-conditioned analysis set) are recorded above but are not the axis on which one would set a contrast.
n_predictions: record the three levels separately. - **Samples per target:** 20. p13: "we generate N = 20 cofolding samples per target for each inference run." Fixed for all targets and all models; no per-target adaptation. - **Targets per model:** 1,420. p13: "Inferences are performed on NVIDIA A100 GPUs across the 1,420 unique configuration pairs (43 apo + 1,377 holo) defined during curation." - **Models:** 3 (Boltz-2, Chai-1, Protenix). - **Total:** **NOT REPORTED by the paper.** 20 × 1,420 × 3 = **85,200** predicted structures by arithmetic from the numbers on p13; this product is derived here, not a figure the authors print. - **Analysed rather than generated:** 950 systems × 20 × 3 = 57,000 structures reach the Figure 2 analysis (derived); 509 systems × ≥10 correct × 3 reach Figure 4; 234 holo/apo pairs × 20 × 3 reach Figure 5. - **Discarded, count NOT REPORTED:** p13, "targets that failed annotation because of malformed outputs or missing motifs are excluded."
si_in_scope: **SI NOT HELD.** The held PDF is main text only (18 pages, ending at the reference list). The paper cites Supplementary Information for: the KinCoRe label format (p4), acronym definitions (p5 caption), the continuous distance/dihedral descriptor definitions (p9), and the KinCoRe pipeline details (p13). It cites **Supplementary Figures S1–S4** — S1 ligand and KinCoRe label frequencies (p5), S2 geometric distributions of successful predictions per model (p6), S3 how the 509 diversity targets distribute across the Top-K benchmark (p9), S4 that all models capture correct *average* distances and angles (p9) — and **Supplementary Tables S1–S4** — S1 the 36-theoretical/12-observed label combinations and Type-I ligand prevalence (p5, p6), S2 the label-validity check (p6), **S3 the exact Top-K success numbers (p7)**, **S4 the 110 joint-failure kinases (p8)**. The most-cited comparator numbers in this note (exact Top-1 and Top-20 accuracies) live in Table S3 and are therefore approximate here, read off Figure 2b. Code and data are stated to be public: https://github.com/THGLab/KinConfBench (p13).

year: 2026 (this version posted May 17, 2026 — p1)
venue: bioRxiv preprint. Footer on every page: "this version posted May 17, 2026 ... (which was not certified by peer review)". Body reads "Preprint." (p1). Tagged `preprint`.
title: "ConforFlux: Particle-Guided Trunk Repulsion for Diverse Protein Conformations" (p1). Matches `refs.bib` exactly.
system: general protein + transporter, with membrane transporters carrying the paper's two headline results. Four ConforMix categories: domain motion (n=38), membrane transporter cycling (n=35 after augmentation), cryptic pocket formation (n=33), fold switching (n=15) — p4–p5, p19. Plus a separate 12-pair post-cutoff transporter arm (p5–p6, p20) and a single-target human dopamine transporter case study (p7, p23). No GPCRs, no protein kinases.
n_targets: **121 (target, category) evaluation rows in the main benchmark; 131 unique proteins across everything (arithmetic, never printed).** - ConforMix: "The four sets total 101 (target, category) pairs over 98 unique proteins, with three proteins appearing in both domain motion and cryptic pockets and evaluated under both protocols" (p19). - Transporter category augmented with "20 within-cutoff pairs from Wu and Feng [2025] (after excluding 5 that overlap with the ConforMix set), bringing it to 35 targets" (p5). 38+35+33+15 = 121 rows in Table 1; Table 2's difficulty bins (49+35+37) corroborate 121. - Post-cutoff arm: 12 EGF transporter pairs (p5, p20). DAT case study: 1 target, "DAT is not in the post-cutoff transporter set" (p7). - Hyperparameter sweep set: 10 targets (p20). - 98 + 20 + 12 + 1 = 131 unique proteins is my arithmetic, not the paper's.
method_class: **other** — inference-time latent-space intervention (trunk-level particle guidance: a pairwise Cα-RMSD repulsion gradient back-propagated onto Boltz-2's trunk single and pair embeddings). "ConforFlux is an inference-time procedure that leaves Boltz-2's weights and inputs unchanged." (p3). Nine baselines *actually run* span MSA-subsampling (CF-random), MSA column masking (AFsample3), MSA clustering (AF-cluster), embedding scaling (Boltz-sample), coordinate guidance (ConforMix-RMSD on Boltz-1 and Boltz-2), and a trained ensemble generator (BioEmu) — p5, p16–p17.
backbones: **Boltz-2 v2.2.1** is the only model modified (p16). Boltz-1 v0.3.0 appears only as the substrate of the ConforMix-RMSD-Boltz-1 baseline, which the authors also port to Boltz-2 precisely so the comparison is backbone-matched (p16, p20). BioEmu is run as a separately trained ensemble generator on the same MSA (p17). AF2-backbone EGF numbers are **cited, not run**: "the original AF2-backbone Entropy Guided Fold (EGF) reported from their Table 3" (p5). `multi-backbone` NOT tagged — see `unresolved` item 3 for the judgement call.
templates: **NOT REPORTED.** The word "template" never appears in the paper outside a reference title (grep over the full text). Table 5 "Base model inference parameters" (p16) lists diffusion steps, recycling, step scale, σ range, σ_data, ρ, γ, noise scale — no template row. The only related statement is "leaves Boltz-2's weights and inputs unchanged" (p3).
msa_handling: **full, fixed, and shared across every arm.** "All methods generate 500 samples per target on the same MSA, computed with the ColabFold MMseqs2 server [Mirdita et al., 2022]." (p16). Subsampling / masking / clustering occur **only inside the MSA baselines** (CF-random depths {2,4,8,16,32,64,128}; AFsample3 mask rate 0.40; AF-cluster DBSCAN with ε chosen to maximise cluster count — Table 7, p17). No state-filtering anywhere: no MSA is ever substituted for a state-specific alignment. ConforFlux itself is explicitly *downstream* of the MSA — "The trunk output lies downstream of the input MSA and upstream of the diffusion module, so the intervention retains the full MSA-derived signal" (p8). - **experimental-method conditioning**: Boltz-2 carries X-ray / MD conditioning at inference; the two default baselines bracket both, and "All other Boltz-2-based methods, including ConforFlux, use X-ray conditioning." (p5).
states_generated: **ensemble + two-state.** The method produces a 500-sample ensemble per target (M=5 particles × 5 σ values × 20 seeds — Table 6, p16), and every headline metric collapses that ensemble onto exactly **two** deposited reference states per target ("Each (target, reference) pair contributes a binary success indicator", p18; "Each target has two experimentally resolved reference conformations", p19). The DAT case study extends to **three** states (outward / occluded / inward), but only under a bandwidth set widened beyond the shipped configuration (p7). The dual form is required because the single-state half is real and load-bearing: under the production σ set the DAT ensemble collapses — "Re-running ConforFlux on DAT with the default σ ∈ {0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5} Å configuration (20 seeds, 5 particles, 500 samples) yields zero confidently-inward predictions" (p25). Note the collapse-onto-one-basin behaviour is also what the *default* Boltz-2 baseline does and what the paper exists to fix: "their default inference samples concentrate around a single dominant conformation" (p1).
structural_priors_used: **Extensive, entirely at design and scoring time; none enters the model's input.** 1. **Every benchmark target exists only because two deposited states exist.** "Each target has two experimentally resolved reference conformations corresponding to distinct functional states." (p19). Sources: BioEmu test split + OC23 (domain motion), IOMemP/TP16 (transporter), BioEmu cryptic-pocket set, Porter & Looger (fold switching) — p19; EGF transporter set of Wu & Feng — p20. 2. **DAT was chosen because the full cycle had just been solved.** "Li et al. [2024] solved five cryo-EM structures of DAT (PDB 8Y2C, 8Y2D, 8Y2E, 8Y2F, 8Y2G) that together capture the outward-facing, occluded, and inward-facing states of the alternating-access cycle, all post-cutoff." (p7). 3. **Curated residue annotations define the scored region for cryptic pockets.** "For cryptic pocket, RMSD is measured on the BioEmu pocket residues after superposition on the BioEmu alignment residues" (p18); Q16539 dropped "because the BioEmu assets carry no pocket annotation for it" (p18). 4. **The DAT mechanism metrics and the superposition scaffold are lifted from the experimental paper.** Four Cα indicators of Li et al. 2024 (TM1a tilt, R85–D476, F76–G425, F76 displacement) — p23–p24; "Each prediction is superimposed onto 8Y2G on the scaffold Cα atoms (TM3, TM4, TM8, TM9; 93 residues from the 8Y2G secondary-structure annotation)" (p23). 5. **Scoring thresholds are calibrated on deposited-pair geometry** (τ, FR eligibility, DAT margin) — see route 4 below, where the same fact is also a leakage route because the calibration set *is* the evaluation set.
oracle_leakage: **PRESENT. Routes 4, 5, 6 and 7 all fire; routes 1, 2 and 3 are genuinely absent.** Protocol pages: p3–p4 (method), p5 (benchmark protocol), p16–p17 (hyperparameters and baselines), p18–p19 (evaluation), p19–p20 (datasets), p20–p22 (ablations), p23–p25 (DAT). **R1 — deposited structures used as input or template: NONE FOUND.** No structure is supplied to the model at any point. "ConforFlux is an inference-time procedure that leaves Boltz-2's weights and inputs unchanged." (p3); "parallel trajectories initialized from the same trunk outputs" with the trunk fed only sequence and MSA (p2, p3). Templates are never mentioned anywhere in the paper (see `templates`), so the route is absent by silence rather than by an explicit templates-off statement. Protocol page for checking: p3 (Section 3.1) and p16 (Table 5). **R2 — state annotations from a curated database (GPCRdb, KLIFS, Kincore) driving templates or alignments: NONE FOUND.** No such database appears. The only curated annotation used anywhere is the BioEmu cryptic-pocket residue list, and it drives the **scoring region only**, not the alignment or any input: "For cryptic pocket, RMSD is measured on the BioEmu pocket residues after superposition on the BioEmu alignment residues [Lewis et al., 2025]." (p18). Protocol pages: p18 (evaluation details), p19–p20 (datasets). **R3 — cluster labels derived from known states: NONE FOUND.** ConforFlux uses no clustering. The AF-cluster baseline clusters the MSA on a structure-free criterion: "DBSCAN clusters the MSA following the original implementation [Wayment-Steele et al., 2024]; the ε that maximizes the cluster count is selected" (Table 7, p17). The DAT PCA is fitted on prediction and reference vectors jointly (p24) but is used for visualisation, with classification done by nearest-reference RMSD (also R6, below). **R4 — hyperparameters, sweep ranges, seeds or stopping criteria tuned against known states: PRESENT, and this is the sharpest finding in the note. There is no held-out or tuning split anywhere in the paper** (grep for "held-out", "validation set", "tuning set", "development set" returns nothing but the DAT boundary-class usage on p24). *(a) The hyperparameter sweep set is drawn from the evaluation benchmark and, worse, is selected by the evaluation outcome itself.* Verbatim, p20: **"We sweep four hyperparameters around the defaults: step size η_s = η_z = 0.02, kernel bandwidth σ = 2.0, particle count M = 5, and update interval k = 3. The sweep uses ten domain-motion and transporter targets under 500 residues, drawn one per decile of the per-target default-vs-ConforFlux improvement."** The stratification variable — per-target default-vs-ConforFlux improvement — is computed from worst-case Cα RMSD to the held reference structures on the benchmark the paper then reports. So the tuning subset is not merely *inside* the evaluation set, it is *chosen using the evaluation result*. *(b) The values reported in that sweep are reference-RMSD values.* Table 10 (p22) scores every condition by "Worst-case alternate-reference Cα Kabsch RMSD" against the deposited alternate state, over the same 10 targets. *(c) The production σ range was fixed by that sweep.* Verbatim, p4: "The bandwidth σ is held constant per particle batch but swept across a small fixed set ({0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5} Å) so that the resulting samples span a range of repulsion radii rather than concentrating at a single σ." Justified at p20: "Performance is flat across σ ∈ [1, 2] and degrades sharply for σ ≥ 4 (kernel saturation)." This is the **schema's explicit route-4 case: a *range* tuned on the evaluation set, with no per-target value chosen.** *(d) The σ range was then widened for one target after the shipped range failed to reach a state the authors knew was there.* Verbatim, p7: **"For this case study we widen the repulsion bandwidth set to σ ∈ [0, 5] Å (Appendix L). The inward basin is reached only at the upper end of this set, beyond the benchmark σ values used in Tables 1 and 2."** Confirmed at p25: "Re-running ConforFlux on DAT with the default σ ∈ {0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5} Å configuration ... yields zero confidently-inward predictions and 90 boundary Inward/Occluded predictions." The DAT inward result — the paper's mechanistic centrepiece — exists only under a per-target hyperparameter change made with the target state in hand. Disclosed cleanly, but it is leakage. *(e) M=5 chosen on a compute/reference-RMSD trade-off, against a sweep that says M=7 is better.* Verbatim, p20–p21: "Success improves monotonically with particle count across M ∈ [3, 7], with diminishing returns; M =5 saves ∼30% compute relative to M =7 at a cost of 0.3 Å alt-RMSD." Table 10 (p22): M=7 gives 2.81 Å worst alt-RMSD vs M=5's 3.11 Å. *(f) The embedding target is chosen against the same 10-target sweep, and the chosen setting is worse than both alternatives on both metrics.* Verbatim, p21: "updating only the pair representation (z̄) achieves the lowest mean worst-case alt-RMSD (2.17 Å, best on 6 of 10 targets) at clashscore 11.3, below the combined update's 12.4. Updating only the single representation (s̄) yields the lowest mean clashscore (9.9) at slightly higher RMSD (2.74 Å). **We use the combined s̄ + z̄ update.**" Table 10 (p22) gives the combined update 3.11 Å and clashscore 12.4 — worse than z-only on RMSD and worse than s-only on clashscore. No justification for the choice is given. *(g) Stopping criterion: **HOW IT WAS CHOSEN IS NOT REPORTED.*** Table 6 (p16) lists "Stop fraction 0.8 — Active for the first 80% of denoising steps". It is not in the sensitivity sweep of Appendix I (which covers only η, σ, M, k — p20), is never justified in text, and no alternative value is reported anywhere. *(h) Metric thresholds calibrated on deposited-pair geometry from the evaluation set.* Verbatim, p18: "Domain motion uses τ = 2.0 Å on the full structure, **tightened from BioEmu's 3 Å for parity with the transporter scale (median inter-reference Cα RMSD 5.20 Å for domain motion vs 4.92 Å for transporter)**." The tightening rationale is a statistic of the held reference pairs. Fill-ratio eligibility likewise: "We therefore restrict FR to targets with T_ref < 0.95 across all categories" (p19), T_ref being the inter-reference TM-score. And the DAT classifier margin: "The margin is necessary because the RMSD between 8Y2D and the nearest inward reference is only 1.15 Å, comparable to Boltz-2's own prediction spread" (p24). *Seeds are clean:* "Seeds 20 — Random seeds (42–61)" (Table 6, p16), fixed and shared with the default baseline's 42–51 (Table 7, p17). **R5 — success defined post hoc by RMSD/TM to a structure they had: PRESENT, and it is every headline number.** Verbatim, p18: "Each (target, reference) pair contributes a binary success indicator 1{min_i RMSD(s_i, r) ≤ τ} over the 500 samples." Verbatim, p19: "RMSD_worst({s_i}) = max( min_i RMSD(s_i, r_1), min_i RMSD(s_i, r_2) ), which indicates whether the sampling distribution reaches both experimentally resolved states or only the dominant one." Fill ratio is TM-score to the two references (p19). The DAT inward count is nearest-reference classification (p24). Every reported success is a best-of-500 max taken against a deposited structure the authors held. The authors state the consequence themselves — see `stated_limits`, p8. **R6 — best/worst model labels assigned against a held reference: PRESENT, and it drives every structure render.** Verbatim, Fig. 1 caption p3: "ConforFlux reaches both references, with **the closest sample to each shown**, mutually aligned and colored by per-residue Cα RMSD." Verbatim, Fig. 2 caption p7: "middle **the best ConforFlux prediction** overlaid on each reference". Verbatim, Fig. 3 caption p8: "bottom **the best ConforFlux prediction** overlaid on each experimental reference." Verbatim, Fig. 4 caption p9: "(B) For each major state, **the best ConforFlux prediction** overlaid on the experimental reference." Also the DAT state labels: "Each prediction is assigned to a state by nearest reference in global Cα RMSD" (p24). The authors flag the limit of this labelling: "The state classifier reflects relative reference proximity, not basin occupancy." (p24). **R7 — design-level oracle use (input conditions or systems chosen because the expected answer is known): PRESENT. Weaker than the pipeline leakage above; label it as design-level.** Every target enters the study only because both states are deposited (see `structural_priors_used` 1). DAT was selected because its full cycle had just been solved (p7). The framing is explicit at p1: "Even when a target's alternate state is well-characterized in the literature, sampling at default settings rarely reaches it." Nothing leaky is fed to the model — the expected state is simply known before the result is read.
prospective: **no.** No arm is prospective. Every target is chosen because both states are deposited (R7); every headline metric is a best-of-500 against those deposited structures (R5); the hyperparameter set was fixed against reference-RMSD on ten targets drawn from the evaluation benchmark by outcome decile (R4a); the σ range was widened for DAT after the shipped range failed to reach the known inward state (R4d). The **post-cutoff arm (12 pairs) is the closest thing to a prospective test and it is genuinely blind at the entry level**, but the authors themselves qualify it: "Homologous transporters in other conformational states may appear in pre-cutoff training data, so this evaluation tests generalization to unseen sequences and entries." (p6). Even there, success is scored against the post-cutoff structures the authors hold, so it is a memorization control rather than a prospective prediction. No structure is predicted before its alternate state was known.
state_metric: **binary predicate + continuous coordinate, both anchored on distance to a deposited reference.** - *Binary predicate — per-state success rate*, at **category-specific thresholds** (p18): domain motion τ = 2.0 Å full structure (tightened from BioEmu's 3 Å, justified by median inter-reference Cα RMSD 5.20 vs 4.92 Å); membrane transporter τ = 2.0 Å full structure (the EGF benchmark threshold of Wu & Feng); cryptic pocket τ = 1.0 Å **on the BioEmu pocket region** (tightened from BioEmu's 1.5 Å "since the metric evaluates only the curated 10–30 pocket residues"); fold switching τ = 3.0 Å full structure (following Wayment-Steele et al.). Post-cutoff transporter arm uses τ = 2.0 Å throughout: "The 2.0 Å success threshold of the original benchmark is applied throughout." (p6). **All four thresholds are justified — an improvement on the usual practice** — but three of the four justifications are inherited from source benchmarks and the fourth is calibrated on the evaluation set's own reference geometry (R4h). - *Continuous — worst-case minimum Cα Kabsch RMSD* over 500 samples (Eq. 3, p19). - *Continuous — fill ratio* (Kalakoti & Wallner), TM-score based, 100 bins along the inter-reference segment, restricted to T_ref < 0.95 (p19). - *Continuous — DAT mechanism metrics*: R85–D476 Cα distance, F76–G425 Cα distance, F76 Cα displacement, TM1a tilt (p23–p24). These are the one place the state is called by something other than reference distance, and they are the reason `rmsd-only` is **not** tagged. - *Classification* — DAT nearest-reference assignment at a 0.3 Å margin, with a boundary class held out (p24). - Statistical treatment: "Succ. is mean ± std over 1000 state-level bootstrap trials" (Table 1 caption, p5); "We resample (target, state) pairs with replacement to obtain 1000 bootstrap replicates" (p19). Post-cutoff arm uses a one-sided Wilcoxon with Bonferroni correction (p6).
metric_saturation: **Yes — three numeric saturations, two of them stated by the authors.** (Axis truncations are recorded in `hides` on the Fig. 5 and Fig. 7 rows, not here.) 1. **The per-state success indicator is explicitly saturated at 500 samples.** Verbatim, p18: "The within-state Monte Carlo variance is essentially saturated at this sample count, so the only meaningful uncertainty is across (target, state) pairs, motivating this deterministic formulation rather than success@N." 2. **Fill ratio degenerates as T_ref → 1, and targets are excluded to avoid it.** Verbatim, p19: "The metric collapses when the inter-reference TM-score T_ref approaches one, because the inter-reference quadrant shrinks to a narrow diagonal band into which almost any plausible fold projects. We therefore restrict FR to targets with T_ref < 0.95 across all categories." 5 of 33 cryptic-pocket targets and 2 of 15 fold-switching targets are dropped on this rule (p19), so the FR column of Table 1 is computed on n = 38 / 35 / 28 / 13 while the Succ. column is on 38 / 35 / 33 / 15. 3. **The easy difficulty stratum is at ceiling.** Table 2 (p6): default (X-ray) 86.7, default (MD) 86.7, CF-random 90.8, ConforFlux 90.8 — the top two methods are tied at the same value and the whole column spans 75.5–90.8. The paper's own summary concedes it: "ConforFlux exceeds default by 4.1 pp on easy targets" versus +13.5 pp on hard (p5). 4. **Granularity, not saturation, but it matters for reading the deltas:** fold switching is n=15 targets → 30 (target, state) pairs → one pair moves the rate 3.3 pp, and the paper's own fold-switching gap is exactly 3.3 pp ("ranks second on fold switching by 3.3 pp", p5), i.e. one (target, state) pair. On the 12-pair post-cutoff arm one target is 8.3 pp. - Separately, the *guidance kernel* saturates at large σ ("degrades sharply for σ ≥ 4 (kernel saturation)", p20), which is a method property, not a metric one.
directional_control: **NONE. The method offers diversity only — it cannot be told which state to produce. The authors say so outright.** **Verbatim, p8:** *"ConforFlux therefore does not prescribe a direction of conformational change. Its repulsion only drives particles apart, and the alternative states come from the trunk itself, leaving the exploration to the model."* **Verbatim, p9 (Conclusion):** *"Because the trunk has been reported to encode more than one conformation, the repulsion only has to drive particles apart, and the model supplies the states themselves."* Handles that exist: kernel bandwidth σ (a repulsion **radius**, not a direction), particle count M, update interval k, step size η, random seed (Table 6, p16). No partner, no ligand, no nanobody, no peptide, no state-annotated template, no state-filtered MSA, no subsample depth. The DAT result makes the distinction concrete: widening σ from {0.5–2.5} to [0, 5] Å was what let samples reach the inward basin (p7, p25) — i.e. the only lever is *how far apart* to push, not *where to go*, and finding the right distance for a target required already knowing the answer.
anti_memorization_design: **PRESENT — 12 post-cutoff transporter pairs, plus a post-cutoff single-target case study.** - *Cutoff definition*: Boltz-2 training cutoff **2023-06-01**, defined as initial PDB release date. Verbatim, p20: "Of the 32 retained, 20 have both references released before the Boltz-2 training cutoff (2023-06-01) [Passaro et al., 2025] and 12 have at least one post-cutoff reference (Table 9)." Restated at p25: "the Boltz-2 cutoff (initial PDB release before 2023-06-01, Passaro et al., 2025)"; the Boltz-1 cutoff (2021-09-30) is given too. - *n and construction*: the EGF set of Wu & Feng has 37 pairs; "We use 32 of the original 37 pairs, excluding slc39, mdfA, AAC3, PF0708, and murJ for overlap with ConforMix transporters." (p20). 20 within-cutoff → folded into the Table 1 Transporter category; **12 post-cutoff → the held-out arm**, listed per target with PDB IDs, lengths and T_ref in Table 9 (p20). - *Definition scope, stated honestly*: "Here 'post-cutoff' refers to the release date of the specific deposited entries. Homologous transporters in other conformational states may appear in pre-cutoff training data, so this evaluation tests generalization to unseen sequences and entries." (p6). - *DAT*: "All five entries were deposited 2024-01-25 and released 2024-08-14, postdating the Boltz-2 training cutoff (2023-06-01)" (p23). - *Within-/post-cutoff split is clean and audited*: "7PQG/7VAG, with both references released in May 2022, is one of the 20 within-cutoff pairs." (p20).
anti_memorization_control: **RUN — a real arm, analysed, with statistics. This is the strongest rigour feature of the paper.** Not `NONE RUN`. - Section 4.2 (p5–p6) runs four configurations on the same 12 post-cutoff pairs. "The three Boltz-2 columns share backbone, MSA, and sample count, so the only varying factor among them is the guidance method." (p6). Aggregate in Table 4 (p7), per-target in Table 9 (p20), per-target scatters in Fig. 14 (p29). - Significance tested: "one-sided Wilcoxon p = 0.0017 vs default, p = 0.0007 vs EGF on Boltz-2, both Bonferroni-significant" (p6). - A **second, homolog-level** memorization control is run on DAT and reported as a *negative* for the authors' own claim (Appendix L.6, p25): "Inward conformations of SLC6 transporters predate both Boltz training cutoffs. The human serotonin transporter inward conformation (PDB 6DZZ, released 2019-04-24) and the bacterial LeuT inward-open conformation (PDB 3TT3, released 2012-01-04) are both before the Boltz-1 cutoff ... and the Boltz-2 cutoff ... The DAT-specific cryo-EM entries 8Y2C/E/F are post-cutoff at the entry level, but the inward conformation type itself is not novel to either model." - **NOT marked `UNPOWERED`** by the schema's rule: n = 12 ≥ ~10, and the set does not overlap training at the entry level. But it is marginal — one target moves the success rate 8.3 pp, so 4/12 → 9/12 is five targets, and the authors' own homolog caveat (p6, p25) means the set is post-cutoff at the *entry* level only, not at the *conformation-type* level.
confidence_as_discriminator: **No — and they tested it and report the negative.** Confidence is never used to select or rank conformations; ConforFlux's 500 samples are reported unfiltered, and ConforMix's confidence filter is explicitly removed for parity (p17, p21). Appendix C (p17) runs the comparison as a quality check: "Per-category medians differ by at most 0.01 and upper 90th-percentiles by at most 0.005. The diversified samples thus remain among the conformations Boltz-2 scores as confidently as its default outputs. At the same time, confidence barely registers the conformational variation ConforFlux introduces". Stated as a limit at p8: "Predictor confidence does not discriminate correct alternative conformations from incorrect ones [Chakravarty et al., 2024], and Boltz-2 confidence barely registers the variation ConforFlux introduces (Appendix C)." Not tagged `confidence-as-discriminator` — see `unresolved` item 4.
stance: **`precedent` on findings + `contrast` on rigour. PROVISIONAL — the user's call.**
n_predictions: - **Samples per target: 500 for every method, everywhere.** "All Boltz-2-based methods use the same model weights and generate 500 samples per target" (p5); "All methods generate 500 samples per target on the same MSA" (p16). - **ConforFlux's 500 decomposes as M=5 particles × 5 σ values × 20 seeds (42–61)** — Table 6, p16. Default baselines decompose as 10 seeds × 50 samples (Table 7, p17). - **Targets**: 121 (target, category) rows in the main benchmark (38 + 35 + 33 + 15), over 98 unique ConforMix proteins + 20 added within-cutoff EGF pairs; 12 post-cutoff pairs; 1 DAT case study; 10 targets in the ablation set. - **Totals are never printed.** My arithmetic: ConforFlux benchmark alone 121 × 500 = 60,500 samples; all ten methods 605,000; post-cutoff arm 3 Boltz-2 configurations × 12 × 500 = 18,000 (AF2-EGF cited only); DAT 3 × 500 = 1,500 (default, ConforFlux extended-σ, ConforFlux production-σ — p23, p25); ablations 10 targets × 50 samples per condition (25 for the adaptive-scaling block) across ~20 conditions (p22).
si_in_scope: **In scope.** Appendices A–M are inside this 29-page PDF (contents list p15) and carry every hyperparameter (Table 6, p16), the full baseline configuration table (Table 7, p17), evaluation definitions (p18–p19), dataset construction and cutoff dates (p19–p20), per-target post-cutoff results (Table 9, p20), the complete ablation table (Table 10, p22) and the DAT measurement protocol (p23–p25). No external supplementary file is cited. **One gap**: per-target values behind Tables 1 and 2 exist only as scatter grids (Figs. 10–13, p26–p29) and are not tabulated, so per-target numbers for the four main categories are not machine-extractable from this PDF; only the 12 post-cutoff targets are tabulated.

venue: bioRxiv preprint. "this version posted January 23, 2026 ... which was not certified by peer review" (p1). Tagged `preprint`.
title: "Steering Conformational Sampling in Boltz-2 via Pair Representation Scaling" (p1). NOTE: `refs.bib` carries a different title ("Biasing Conformational Sampling in AlphaFold 3 and Boltz-2 via Pair Representation Scaling"). The PDF title is authoritative; see `unresolved`.
system: general protein + transporter. Three datasets: OC23 (open/closed proteins), TP16 (membrane transporters, inward/outward-facing), MS15 (curated panel spanning "six functional categories, including a kinase, GTPases, periplasmic binding proteins, fold-switching proteins, membrane transporters, and an intramembrane protease", p9). Transporters are the plurality: TP16 entirely, plus 6 of 15 MS15 targets (Table 2, p10). No GPCRs.
n_targets: 58 total across three datasets — OC23 = 23 proteins (p9); TP16 = 20 sequences after excluding SPF1, evaluated at construct level (p3, p9); MS15 = 15 targets (p4, Table 2 p10). Combined n = 58 is corroborated by p5 ("18 targets (31% of the combined dataset)"; 18/0.31 ≈ 58) but the number 58 is never printed.
method_class: other — inference-time latent-space intervention (uniform scalar rescaling of the Pairformer pair representation), not an input perturbation. Baseline arms actually run include MSA-subsampling, MSA random masking, and MSA clustering (AF-Cluster-inspired), plus a "Laplacian" spatially-structured scaling ablation (p9–p11).
backbones: Boltz-2 version 2.1.1 (p12) is the only model modified. AlphaFold 3 Server is run as an external reference at default settings, 5 models per target (p3, p10, Table 3 p11). Two backbones, so `multi-backbone` NOT tagged (schema requires more than two head to head).
templates: off. "All Boltz-2 based methods were run without input templates to strictly evaluate the sampling capabilities." (p10). Template usage inside the AF3 Server arm is NOT REPORTED.
msa_handling: full (fixed, shared across methods) for the primary method; subsampled / masked / clustered only in the baseline arms; sequence-only in an ablation. "Input MSAs were collected from the AlphaFold3 server [16] (Fig. 7). To strictly isolate the contribution of sampling strategies, we utilized these fixed MSAs across all benchmarked methods" (p9). No state-filtering anywhere — the MSA is never substituted for a state-specific alignment. Subsampling is p ∈ {0.05, 0.10, …, 0.50} (Table 3, p11).
states_generated: ensemble (500 models per target for Boltz-sample), evaluated as two states. Both discrete and continuous responses are reported: "For adenylate kinase (P69441), the ensemble shifts smoothly with β, tracing a continuum between the two conformations. In contrast, the ADP/ATP translocase (G2QNH0) and EF-Tu (P0CE48) exhibit a more discrete, mode-switching response" (p5).
structural_priors_used: **New in v3. Two kinds, and the paper's central claim is about the second.** 1. **Design-time, in the benchmark.** OC23 and TP16 are inherited wholesale from the AFsample2 benchmark, *"datasets from the AFsample2 benchmark [10] that provide paired reference structures for distinct conformational states such as open/closed or outward/inward-facing forms."* (p3); TP16 is re-cut at construct level to 20 sequences after excluding the very long SPF1 (p3). MS15 is curated by the authors against a pairwise TM-score ≤ 0.85 criterion. Every target therefore has both states deposited before a single prediction is made, and the worked example is scored against PDB **3TEE** and **3VJP** (p2). No deposited structure enters the pipeline. 2. **Inside the model, and this is the argument.** The paper's causal story is that β-scaling exposes structural knowledge Boltz-2 already holds, rather than amplifying coevolutionary signal. Verbatim, p1: *"our analysis of sequence-only inference reveals that the method does not rely solely on coevolutionary signals but actively unlocks the structural priors internalized by the model to recover alternative states even without MSA information."* Restated at p5: *"internal scaling does not merely randomize the output, but effectively leverages the model's internalized structural priors to recover alternative conformations even without explicit coevolutionary signals."* **Why the two interact badly.** The mechanism the authors propose is memorised structural priors, and the benchmark contains no memorisation control (see `anti_memorization_control`). The paper's explanation and its largest methodological gap are therefore the same fact seen from two sides, which is worth saying plainly whenever it is cited.
oracle_leakage: **PRESENT — six routes, none of which is "best β picked per target by agreement with a known structure".** Enumerated separately below. Protocol pages: p9 (β sweep and datasets), p10 (baselines, MSA source), p11–p12 (metrics and selection). **R1 — β sweep range chosen empirically on the same benchmarks used for evaluation (the field flagged in the task).** Verbatim, p9: "We swept β from −0.75 to 0.75 in fixed increments. This range was empirically determined to maximize the exploration of conformational diversity while preventing projection collapse or severe steric clashes associated with extreme interaction strengths." Verbatim, p3: "In practice, we swept β over a moderate range that preserves stable inference while measurably shifting the generated ensemble." **How the scalar was selected, precisely**: (i) the *range* [−0.75, +0.75] is a global hyperparameter stated to be "empirically determined", with no held-out or tuning split described anywhere in Methods; the stated selection criteria are "conformational diversity" and avoidance of "projection collapse or severe steric clashes". In this paper conformational diversity is only ever operationalised as ΔTM range and fill-ratio, both of which are computed **against the two deposited reference structures** (p11–p12). So the range was tuned against reference-dependent quantities measured on the evaluation sets themselves. (ii) A *single best β* is never chosen. All 10 β values (β ∈ {±0.15, …, ±0.75}, β = 0 excluded as it duplicates vanilla; Table 3, p11) are pooled into the 500-model ensemble, and the paper explicitly disclaims any β→state mapping: "Accordingly, we do not observe a consistent mapping between the sign of β and a particular conformational state across datasets." (p6). (iii) Prospective per-target *model* selection is by mean pLDDT, not by reference agreement (p12). Net: **leakage at the level of the global hyperparameter range and of the tuning-set/evaluation-set identity, not at the level of a per-target oracle β.** **R2 — success is defined post hoc as best-of-N agreement with the held reference structures.** Verbatim, p11: "we identified the best-scoring model for each reference structure independently. Given a target with two experimentally determined states (denoted as reference 1 and reference 2), we computed the maximum TM-score achieved within the ensemble for each state, TMmax_ref1 and TMmax_ref2. We report the Best minimum TM-score as min(TMmax_ref1, TMmax_ref2)". Verbatim, p11: "Dual-state coverage is defined as the percentage of targets for which both TMmax_ref1 and TMmax_ref2 exceed a threshold of 0.8." Every headline number (dual-state coverage, best-min TM, fill-ratio) is a max over 500 samples taken against a structure the authors held. **R3 — an explicit oracle selector is run as an arm (disclosed as an upper bound, not hidden).** Verbatim, p12: "These strategies were benchmarked against an oracle selector that identifies the sampled model maximizing the minimum TM-score to both reference states." Verbatim, p7: "sign-based selection achieved an AUC of 0.58 on MS15, closely tracking the oracle upper bound of 0.60". **R4 — dataset construction requires both deposited states; MS15 targets were curated on a structure-similarity criterion.** Verbatim, p4: "we assembled the MS15 dataset, a curated panel of 15 proteins characterized by distinct conformational states (pairwise TM-score ≤ 0.85)." Verbatim, p9: "Sequences were obtained from UniProt [31], and experimental structures for the alternative states were taken from the RCSB Protein Data Bank (PDB) [32]." Verbatim, p9: "OC23 includes 23 proteins with open and closed states satisfying a pairwise TM-score ≤ 0.85." No state-annotated database (GPCRdb / KLIFS / Kincore) is used, and none of these structures enters the pipeline as input or template. **R5 — post hoc labelling of β direction and of "representative" models against the known references.** Verbatim, p6: "we compute a per-β bias score, b(β) = TMref1(β) − TMref2(β), and visualize b(β) as heatmaps (Fig. 6A)." Verbatim, p5: "For EF-Tu, negative β favors the 1OB2-like state in Fig. 4." Verbatim, p5: "for the transcription factor RfaH (P0AFW0), default inference is concentrated near the β-barrel state (PDB 6C6S), and positive scaling (β > 0) shifts sampling toward the alternative α-helical hairpin state (PDB 2OUG)." Verbatim, Fig. 4 caption p6: "For each target, representative models from distinct conformational regimes are superimposed." **R6 — model-level memorization of the target states, asserted by the authors as the mechanism, with no cutoff control.** Verbatim, p8: "our findings suggest that Boltz-2 has internalized a rich set of structural priors from the PDB training distribution. In this context, β-scaling acts not merely as a noise generator but as a probe that unlocks these latent priors, allowing the model to access alternative states that are suppressed under standard inference conditions." Verbatim, p5: "This systematic skew toward higher accuracy indicates that internal scaling does not merely randomize the output, but effectively leverages the model's internalized structural priors to recover alternative conformations even without explicit coevolutionary signals." The reference structures (Table 2, p10: 4AKE/1AKE, 2OUG/6C6S, 2QKE/5JYT, 1OMP/1ANF, …) are deposited PDB entries; the Boltz-2 training cutoff is never stated and no overlap analysis is performed. **Routes explicitly ABSENT (checkable negatives):** no deposited structure is supplied as input or template — "All Boltz-2 based methods were run without input templates to strictly evaluate the sampling capabilities." (p10); no state-filtered or state-annotated MSA — the same fixed AF3-server MSA is used for every method (p9); the clustering baseline's own hyperparameter is chosen on a structure-free criterion — "We varied eps from 0.05 to 0.50 and selected the value that maximized the number of clusters." (p11).
prospective: **partial.** Prospective in the sampling stage and in one selection arm — β is applied blind to all targets, no reference structure enters inference, and the confidence-based selectors use mean pLDDT only ("To assess practical utility without reliance on reference structures, we evaluated heuristics based on model confidence", p12). Retrospective everywhere else: the β range is tuned on the evaluation benchmarks (R1), all reported metrics are best-of-500 against held references (R2), the targets exist in the benchmark only because both states are deposited (R4), and the authors attribute the mechanism to memorized PDB priors (R6). No target is modelled before its alternative state was known.
state_metric: continuous coordinate + binary predicate, both anchored on RMSD-free structural similarity to deposited references. - TM-score to each of two reference structures, computed with US-align (p11). - Best minimum TM-score = min(TMmax_ref1, TMmax_ref2) — "quantifies the prediction quality for the harder-to-sample conformation" (p11). - Dual-state coverage = binary predicate at **TM-score ≥ 0.8** for both states (p3, p11). **Threshold justification: NOT REPORTED** — 0.8 is asserted without argument. The related dataset-construction threshold (states must have pairwise TM ≤ 0.85, p4/p9) is also unjustified, and note the two thresholds are only 0.05 apart. - Fill-ratio: models projected onto the diagonal segment between the two references in (TMref1, TMref2) space, N = 100 bins, symmetric parabolic weighting favouring the end bins; "the weighted fraction of bins that contained at least one model" (p12). Adapted from AFsample2. - ΔTM range (ensemble spread) and per-β bias b(β) = TMref1(β) − TMref2(β) (p6). - Success curves: fraction of targets with min(TMref1, TMref2) ≥ t, swept over t (p6).
metric_saturation: **Yes, ceiling on OC23, plus pervasive axis truncation.** - Verbatim ceiling, p3: "On OC23, all methods achieved high best-minimum TM-scores with medians near 0.9. Boltz-sample slightly improved accuracy relative to vanilla and performed comparably to MSA clustering." A best-of-500 max statistic against a reference is structurally ceiling-prone, and on OC23 it has already saturated for every arm, which is why the OC23 accuracy comparison is uninformative and the paper's argument shifts to spread/fill-ratio. - Dual-state coverage is a hard-thresholded binary predicate (TM ≥ 0.8) over 15–23 targets, so it moves in steps of 4.3–6.7 percentage points and cannot resolve small differences. - **Axis truncations** (read from rendered pages): Fig. 2 and Fig. 3 best-min TM-score box panels do not start at 0 (OC23 panel runs ~0.7–1.0); Fig. 2/3 TM-score scatter panels are truncated to ~0.4–1.0 on both axes; Fig. 4 per-target scatters are truncated to narrow target-specific windows (e.g. 0.66–0.98 for P69441, 0.53–0.91 for P0AFW0); Fig. 5 best-min TM-score axis starts at 0.4; Fig. 6B x-axis starts at 0.5. Computation-time panels use a log axis (Fig. 2, Fig. 3), which visually compresses a difference the text states as "less than 10⁻² s per prediction" versus clustering (p3).
directional_control: **Partial and, by the authors' own statement, not state-addressable.** The handle is the sign and magnitude of the scalar β applied to the pair representation — not a partner, ligand, nanobody, peptide, template, or state-filtered MSA. Two directions exist and are useful: "the sign of β effectively defines distinct search directions in the latent space" (p7). But which physical state each direction reaches is target-dependent and not predictable: "Many targets show systematic changes in bias as β varies, but the direction of the shift depends on the target: increasing β can favor either reference state depending on the system. Accordingly, we do not observe a consistent mapping between the sign of β and a particular conformational state across datasets." (p6). So the method can be instructed *to explore in two directions*, but cannot be instructed *to produce a named state*. Secondary handles held fixed: 5 seeds × 10 diffusion samples (Table 3, p11).
anti_memorization_design: **NONE.** No held-out set, no post-cutoff set, no training-cutoff date for Boltz-2 stated anywhere, no PDB-release-date filter on the benchmark targets. MS15 was curated from the PDB with no recency criterion — the stated selection rule is only "distinct conformational states (pairwise TM-score ≤ 0.85)" (p4) and "experimental structures for the alternative states were taken from the RCSB Protein Data Bank (PDB)" (p9). OC23/TP16 are inherited wholesale from AFsample2 (p9). Some MS15 references are recent depositions (8Y5Y/8Y5Z, 8J7X/8J7W, 7AAR, 6N3I; Table 2 p10) but the paper never identifies them as such or uses them as a recency stratum.
anti_memorization_control: **NONE RUN.** The one ablation that touches memorization is the sequence-only (no-MSA) arm, and it is run in the *opposite* direction — as evidence that memorized priors are doing useful work, not as a control against them: "our findings suggest that Boltz-2 has internalized a rich set of structural priors from the PDB training distribution" (p8); "18 targets (31% of the combined dataset) improved by at least 0.05, whereas only a single target (1.7%) worsened by the same margin" (p5). No arm stratifies results by deposition date, training-set membership, or sequence novelty. The gap is load-bearing here because the paper's own causal story (R6) is memorization.
confidence_as_discriminator: **Yes, and partially validated — but validated for ranking, not for judging conformational correctness.** "Given the monomeric nature of the targets, we used the mean pLDDT score as the ranking metric." (p12); ipTM/pTM are not used (monomers). Validation is via success curves against an oracle upper bound and a random baseline: "despite being restricted to just two candidates, sign-based selection achieved an AUC of 0.58 on MS15, closely tracking the oracle upper bound of 0.60 and significantly outperforming the random baseline of 0.47 (Fig. 6B)" (p7). What is NOT validated: that pLDDT distinguishes state 1 from state 2, or that a high-pLDDT model is in the correct basin — pLDDT is only used to pick the single best model *within* each β-sign pool, after the sign has already defined the split. The "significantly" at p7 is not backed by a named test or p-value for the AUC comparison.
stance: **`precedent` + `contrast`** — PROVISIONAL, user's call.
n_predictions: - Samples per target: Boltz-sample (Uniform) **500** = 5 independent seeds × 10 diffusion samples × 10 β values, with β = 0 excluded ("We excluded β = 0 from this set as it duplicates the vanilla inference", p10; Table 3 p11). Boltz-sample (Laplacian) 500. Vanilla **50** (5 seeds × 10 samples). MSA subsampling 500, MSA masking 500, MSA clustering 500 (k = 10 clusters). AF3 Server **5**. Implied ~50 models per β per target. - Targets: 23 (OC23) + 20 (TP16, SPF1 excluded) + 15 (MS15) = 58. - Total predictions across all arms and datasets: **NOT REPORTED**. The paper never sums them, and the sequence-only and Laplacian arms make the total ambiguous. - Hardware/version: Boltz-2 v2.1.1, one NVIDIA RTX A6000 + Intel Xeon Silver 4314 (p12).
si_in_scope: **New in v3. Everything is in the main text — unusually, and to the paper's credit.** No appendix, supplementary information or supplementary table is referenced anywhere in the body; the β sweep and dataset definitions (p9), the baselines and MSA source (p10), the metrics and selection strategies (pp11–12) and the MS15 target table (Table 2, p10) are all in the 15-page main document. **`SI NOT HELD` does not apply here**, and no number quoted from this paper depends on material the corpus lacks. This is the only note in the corpus that can say that without qualification.
